build.summary: Copier is a slit-scan photocopier drawn on one sheet. The light bar is the boundary: rows above it are the toner copy, and below it the colour original still sits live on the glass. Each frame the engine records the original's pose (position, angle, scale), timestamped from coalesced pointer events, into a 1280-row float "pose ledger" texture. Every new row the bar crosses gets the pose from the moment the light passed it, with rotation stored as an angle so fast twists don't tear. A raw WebGL2 fragment shader then rebuilds the copy from that ledger with toner thresholding, 1px edge fill, 1.5px grain, drum streaks along x, paper fibre, a 0.3° skew and a thin line along the original's edge. There are four presets: Xerox, a two-ink misregistered Riso, Fax with row banding, and blue-line Diazo. A finished pass holds for a moment, then the sheet drops 24px and flies on a 420ms / 0.18 spring into a tray that fans out. "Copy the copy" puts the latest sheet back on the glass and runs another pass. The generation counter rolls up, and each generation adds threshold creep, blur and stronger streaks, so the picture slowly turns into a black toner silhouette. Inputs: drag with inertia, wheel or two-finger twist and pinch, grab the bar to carry the scan yourself (it never goes backwards, and the motor ramps back in over 200ms), Space and Enter, arrow keys, and dropping in your own image. Rendering only loops while something moves, pauses when the tab is hidden or the sheet is off screen, steps its pixel ratio down on slow frames, and falls back to Canvas2D without WebGL2.
build.wowMoment: You don't have to touch anything for the first frame. Honus Wagner's card is already 56% copied, and the black-toner top half is bent into an S-curve, outline and all, because the original sways on the glass while the mint light bar keeps moving down. Cause and effect sit on one line. Then hit Enter a few times: each copy goes back on the glass, the Generation counter rolls up, and the face breaks down into a solid black toner silhouette.
build.knownIssues: Nothing was run in a browser, as the rules required; all three checks pass. To check the look I ported the shader to numpy (scratchpad copier_sim.py) and rendered the first frame, all four presets and six generations offline. They read as intended: an S-curved toner copy, Riso pink and blue, no dot screens. Still unverified at runtime: the DOM layout and CSS, the flight-to-tray landing alignment, two-finger twist on a real phone, the Canvas2D fallback, and the synthesised motor sound level. Choices to know about: I followed the engineer's upgrade and used one sheet with the bar as the boundary instead of two panes, so the brief's 640px platen-above-copy layout doesn't apply. The default original is the sharp 660px Wagner card; John, Paul and George are thumbnails and look soft on the platen because the source images are 200px. The `embedded` mode is not implemented, since lab pieces aren't embedded. Spotify covers are not used; you can drop in your own image instead. Only the last 6 copies keep full resolution, so older tray sheets can't go back on the glass. A wheel over the sheet rotates the picture instead of scrolling the page. Sound starts on the first gesture, can be turned off under "Tune the toner", and the scripted first pass is silent.

critique.firstFrame:
Server render shows the light page: title, one-line instruction, a 4:5 grey platen with the T206 Wagner card centred (the CSS fallback), the panel and an empty tray. The engine mounts, decodes the card and immediately prefills 56% of the sheet with a scripted sway ledger. The canvas then fades in over 900ms on top of the fallback, which matches it pixel for pixel, so nothing jumps. The frame that gets the vote is strong: the top half is black toner on off-white paper with the card's outline and figure bent into a clear S-wave (about 39 css px of amplitude plus 3 degrees of twist). The lid-edge line prints as a wavy rule. The bottom half is the full-colour card still swaying live on the grey glass, and a mint lamp line with a white core sits between them. Cause and effect show in one view.

The weakness is how long it lasts. The pass finishes about 1.2s after load, holds for 950ms, then the copy lifts off and flies into a 148px tray. From about 2.2s on, the hero stage is a plain colour card on grey with a faint line at the top. Nothing printed is left on the glass, so a vote taken a few seconds in sees the least interesting state.
critique.checks:
All three pass:
1. `node scripts/lab-gate.mjs copier` printed `PASS  copier`.
2. `compile-check.mjs copier` printed `PASS  compile copier (13 modules)`.
3. `glsl-check.mjs src/app/lab/copier` printed `ok` for both shader templates, copierShader.js:1 (vertex) and :10 (fragment). They contain no `${}` interpolations, so the check is meaningful.

I also checked by hand:
- Every token used in copier.css exists in globals.css.
- SlotNumber has a default export and takes `className`.
- The WebGL2 calls are valid: the RGBA32F ledger uses NEAREST plus texelFetch, the texSubImage2D call with srcOffset is correct, and mipmaps on an NPOT RGBA8 texture are allowed.
- The bake readback flip is correct.
- The DOM, shader and Canvas2D inverse-affine maths agree.
- The pose trail is sampled per row by event timestamp, using coalesced events, and rotation is interpolated by angle.

No blocker found.

issues.problem: The finished copy is auto-ejected 950ms after the pass. The glass then goes back to a plain colour card on grey with no toner on it, so the wow is gone about 2.2s after load. Preset chips and toner dials also have no visible effect while idle, because nothing printed is on the glass. Clicking Riso changes only the chip.
issues.fix: Leave the finished copy on the glass in the 'hold' phase indefinitely and keep rendering it live through the shader, so presets and dials restyle it in place. Eject only on the next pointerdown, Space, Enter, or a source change. Move `renderer.bake` from finishPass to eject so the tray thumbnail matches the preset in use when the copy leaves.

issues.problem: When the autoplay pass ends, a visitor's first instinct is to drag the picture, but in the idle phase that prints nothing. The visitor has to find Copy or Space first, then drag, which splits the mechanic into two steps and delays the moment of cause and effect.
issues.fix: In onPointerDown, when `phase === 'idle'` and the press is on the picture, eject any held copy and call startPass() before taking the pointer. The first drag then prints immediately. Keep Space and Copy for hands-off passes.

issues.problem: In the desktop grid (container wider than 960px), the sheet width comes only from viewport height. On a tall, medium-width box, such as a 1024x1366 iPad in portrait or a 1100x1000 window, the minimum track sum is 208+688+148+112+64 = 1220px. That is wider than the container, and with `justify-content: center` plus `overflow-x: clip` the head/panel column and the tray get clipped on both sides.
issues.fix: Set the sheet size on `.copier__layout`, where cqw resolves against `.copier`: `--copier-sheet-h: min(clamp(360px, calc(100dvh - 136px), 860px), calc((100cqw - 552px) * 1.25));`. Alternatively, raise the stacking breakpoint to `@container (max-width: 1220px)`.

issues.problem: The DPR cap tests `cssWidth < 640`, which is the sheet width, not the viewport width. The sheet is under 640px on almost every laptop (viewport heights below about 936px), so Retina MacBooks render at DPR 1.5, which then gets upscaled. That softens exactly the toner grain, edge fill and streak detail the piece depends on.
issues.fix: Key the cap off the device instead: `const cap = window.matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches || window.innerWidth < 640 ? 1.5 : 2;`.

issues.problem: If the tab is hidden or the sheet scrolls offscreen mid-pass, resume() cancels rAF but leaves the motor noise and hum gains at their pass level. The AudioContext keeps running, so the copier keeps droning in the background tab until the visitor returns. The context is also never suspended while idle.
issues.fix: In resume(), when `!visible || !onscreen`, call `sound.drive(0)`. Give createCopierSound a `sleep()` that runs `context.suspend()` (and `resume()` from wake()). Call it on hidden and on entering idle, and call wake() again when a pass starts.

issues.problem: Every frame re-runs the full toner shader over the whole printed area: 5 to 10 textureLod taps, 4-octave fbm1, 4-octave fbm2 paper and noise2, about 1.9M px at DPR 2. Yet only the band of about 8 rows above the lamp has changed. The brief planned a cached print target, and `preserveDrawingBuffer: true` (line 56) adds a buffer copy every frame for no benefit.
issues.fix: Bake the toner pass into an RGBA8 print target band by band, using a scissor on [prevRow, row) and recomputing the whole target only when params or the preset change. Composite that texture plus the live platen in the display pass. Drop preserveDrawingBuffer, since bake reads from its own FBO.

issues.problem: Eject stacks three synchronous main-thread jobs on one frame: a 5MB readPixels with a new ImageData (from finishPass), a 1024x1280 to 384x480 JPEG toDataURL in makeThumb, and a 1216x1520 flight canvas at DPR 2 that is bigger than the sheet itself. The first frames of the spring flight can hitch.
issues.fix: Use the 1024x1280 sheet canvas, or an ImageBitmap of it, as the flight node directly and scale it with CSS instead of redrawing it at DPR. Build the thumbnail with `createImageBitmap(sheet, {resizeWidth: 384})` after the flight lands. Reuse one ImageData in CopierGL.bake.

issues.problem: The wheel handler always calls preventDefault. In the stacked layout (960px and below), where the page scrolls, a trackpad scroll that passes over the sheet is captured and rotates the picture. It also kills the scripted sway.
issues.fix: Only capture the wheel when ctrlKey or metaKey is held, or while the pointer is inside the original (`insideOriginal(event.clientX, event.clientY)`). Otherwise let the page scroll.

issues.problem: Below 960px the tray sits under the panel, off the bottom of the screen. Ejected copies fly off the bottom edge to a pile the visitor cannot see, and the Copies count and Copy the copy are far from the glass.
issues.fix: In the stacked layout, put a compact tray row (count plus the top 3 sheets at 48px) directly under the sheet, before the panel, so the eject lands on screen.

issues.problem: Each arrow key adds 0.5*pxPerCss sheet px/ms of velocity, about 500 css px/s, which coasts roughly 120px with a 240ms tau and accumulates on key repeat. That is a shove, not a nudge.
issues.fix: Use `(event.shiftKey ? 0.24 : 0.08) * k` and cap the speed with `velocity.x = clamp(velocity.x, -1.2*k, 1.2*k)` (and the same for y).

issues.problem: The `[data-near]` rule comes after `[data-dragging]` and has the same specificity. If the drag starts near the bar, the cursor shows ns-resize while the visitor is actually dragging the picture.
issues.fix: Add `.copier-sheet[data-dragging="true"][data-near="true"] { cursor: grabbing; }`, or call setNear(0) in onPointerDown when taking the picture path.

issues.problem: The ledger texture starts as zeros. With reduced motion, the first pass starts from row 0, and while scan is between 0.4 and 1, ledgerAt reads row 0 with pose.w = 0. That divides by zero in toLocal, so the top pixel row renders NaN garbage for a few frames.
issues.fix: After creating it, initialise the ledger with identity poses (x=W/2, y=H/2, angle 0, scale 1), or use `max(pose.w, 1e-3)` in toLocal and the lod calculation.

issues.problem: The 'The tray is empty' label in a sunken box repeats 'Copies 0' directly above it. Herb's taste bans micro-labels that explain what is already visible.
issues.fix: Remove the text and leave a quiet sunken 4:5 slot, or a hairline outline, as the empty pile.

issues.problem: The Space and Enter key hints show on phones, where there is no keyboard, and widen the two action buttons.
issues.fix: Hide `.copier-kbd` under `@media (pointer: coarse)`.

issues.problem: The file input is visually hidden but still tabbable. When it takes keyboard focus, no ring appears, because `:focus-visible` targets the label and not the input.
issues.fix: Add `.copier-link:has(.copier-file:focus-visible) { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }`.

issues.problem: `--copier-lamp` and `--copier-ease-carriage` are defined but never used. They are leftover slop.
issues.fix: Delete both custom properties.

critique.wowGap: Make the glass never idle. When a pass finishes, leave the copy on the glass, still rendered live by the shader, instead of auto-ejecting it after 950ms. Then the vote frame stays up, and the preset chips and toner dials restyle the copy visibly in place. The visitor's next touch does the rest: grabbing the picture, Space or Enter bakes and lifts the sheet into the tray and starts the next pass at once. Every drag then prints, and every print ends in the satisfying lift-off into the tray.

changes: copierEngine.js: the finished copy now stays on the glass in 'hold' indefinitely, still drawn live by the shader, so the preset chips and dials restyle it in place. The HOLD_MS auto-eject is gone, and the loop sleeps once the glow, fresh fade and sway have settled.

copierEngine.js: the bake moved from finishPass into eject(). The tray sheet now matches whatever preset is in use when it leaves. eject() also starts a quick 240ms lamp return when a pass is queued (QUICK_RETURN_MS in copierMotion.js replaces HOLD_MS).

copierEngine.js: in onPointerDown, pressing in hold or return, or pressing on the picture while idle, ejects the held copy and starts a pass before it takes the pointer, so the first drag prints. It also calls setNear(0), which fixes the ns-resize cursor during a picture drag. Space and Copy still run hands-off passes.

copierEngine.js: added takeHeld() and snapshot(). In hold, Enter feeds the copy on the glass straight back in as the next original with no gap, and loadSource treats fromHeld as a silent clear rather than a second eject. Save PNG in hold saves the sheet on the glass.
copierEngine.js: the DPR cap now keys off the device: (pointer: coarse) or innerWidth < 640 gets 1.5, everything else gets 2.

copierEngine.js: resume() calls sound.drive(0) and sound.sleep() when the tab is hidden or the sheet is offscreen, and rouses the sound on return if a pass is running. Entering hold or idle puts the sound to sleep, and startPass rouses it.

copierEngine.js: the wheel is captured only when ctrl or meta is held, or when the pointer is over the original outside hold. The rect is refreshed on every wheel event. Otherwise the page scrolls and the scripted sway keeps going.

copierEngine.js: the arrow nudge is now 0.08k, or 0.24k with Shift, with velocity capped at plus or minus 1.2k. When the loop restarts after sleeping, its clock resets, so the first rows of a pass no longer sample stale trail times. A queued pass that fails to start falls back to idle cleanly.

copierSound.js: added sleep(), which fades the gains and then suspends the AudioContext after 260ms, and rouse(), which resumes only a context that already exists. thunk now waits for resume. dispose clears the sleep timer.

copierShader.js: split into PRINT_FRAGMENT (the toner, with a uFlip option for the bake) and a light DISPLAY_FRAGMENT. The display program draws the live platen, a texelFetch of the cached print, the fresh fade and the lamp. toLocal, spread and lod now use max(pose.w, 1e-3).

CopierGL.js: the toner pass now renders into a print target the size of the canvas. Each frame only the new band of rows is drawn, scissored to [prevRow, row). The whole target is redrawn only when a 22-value key (params, preset, seed, palette, source) changes, or on resize or context restore. preserveDrawingBuffer was dropped, the ledger texture starts as identity poses, and the bake renders flipped straight into one reused ImageData with no per-row copy loop.
Copier2D.js (the fallback when WebGL2 is unavailable): the preset filter and paper colour now apply at render and bake time through a multiply composite, so presets restyle a held copy there too.

copierFlight.js: the 1024x1280 sheet canvas itself is the flight node, scaled with CSS. A stamp makes settleNode skip a node that has started a newer flight, and earlier animations are cancelled before reuse.

CopierExperience.jsx: tray thumbnails are built after the flight lands, using createImageBitmap at 384x480 and toBlob, then shown as object URLs. The flight node stays up until the thumbnail has painted. Thumbnail URLs are revoked when copies are trimmed and on unmount, and flights still in the air are removed on unmount.
CopierExperience.jsx: 'Copy the copy' and Save now work in hold. A fed copy goes into the tray with a scale-and-blur entrance instead of a flight.
CopierTray.jsx: removed the 'The tray is empty' label, so the empty pile is a quiet sunken 4:5 slot. Save is enabled through a canSave prop.
CopierStage.jsx: the API exposes takeHeld and snapshot, and the aria-label is updated.
copier.css: --copier-sheet-h now lives on .copier__layout as min(clamp(360px, 100dvh - 136px, 860px), (100cqw - 552px) * 1.25), which fixes the desktop-grid clipping on tall, medium-width containers.
copier.css: below 960px, the tray is a compact row directly under the sheet and above the panel: a 48px pile showing the top 3 sheets that fans sideways, the copy count, and Save.

copier.css: added a grabbing cursor for dragging while near the bar and a grab cursor on the handle in hold. Key hints are hidden under (pointer: coarse). The file-input label gets a :has(:focus-visible) focus ring. Removed the unused --copier-lamp and --copier-ease-carriage, and turned off the fed-copy entrance under reduced motion.

polish.remaining: All three checks pass: lab-gate PASS, compile-check PASS (13 modules), and glsl-check ok on all three shader strings. Every listed issue was implemented. No browser was run, by instruction, so everything was verified by tracing the code by hand. Things worth a live look: (1) the seam when Enter swaps the toner display for the baked sheet used as the new original; the baked sheet is 1024 px wide and is upscaled slightly at DPR 2. (2) The cost of a full print-target redraw while a toner dial is being dragged, at DPR 2. (3) The bake still does one synchronous 5MB readPixels on the press that lifts the copy off. (4) Minor: if more than 40 copies are made, a few thumbnail blob URLs for trimmed copies are released only on unmount. Files are in /Users/herb/Documents/GitHub/portfolio/src/app/lab/copier/: copierEngine.js, CopierGL.js, copierShader.js, Copier2D.js, copierSound.js, copierFlight.js, copierMotion.js, CopierExperience.jsx, CopierTray.jsx, CopierStage.jsx, copier.css and experiment.json.

recheck.firstFrame: A single 4:5 sheet of cool platen glass (#e6eaef) sits between a quiet left column and the tray. The top 56% is already printed in black toner on off-white paper: Honus Wagner's T206 card (the default is the card, not John), with the face and shoulders swayed into a clear S-curve of about ±44 css px and ±3°, with grain, drum streaks and a dark lid line at the card edge. A white core with a green-tinted halo marks the light bar at the boundary, with the ink grip on the right. Below the bar, the live colour card is still swaying, so the copy is continuous with the original at the bar and cause and effect read on one line. The pass finishes about 1.2s later, and the full toner copy then stays on the glass indefinitely (hold), so the vote frame lasts. Two flaws: for about 900ms the canvas fades in over the static CSS fallback image, which sits offset from the swaying GL card, so a ghosted double card is briefly visible. And during that first pass the Copy button is sunken-disabled and all seven source thumbnails are greyscale-disabled, so the chrome in the very first frame looks switched off.
recheck.checks: gate: PASS (lint, comments, type system, tokens). compile: PASS (13 modules bundled). glsl: ok for all three shaders in copierShader.js (COPIER_VERTEX at line 1, PRINT_FRAGMENT at line 10, DISPLAY_FRAGMENT at line 213). Nothing is interpolated, so the check is meaningful. All five round-1 issues are verified fixed. (1) finishPass now goes to an indefinite 'hold', the print restyles live on preset and dial changes through printStale and requestRender, and bake runs at eject. (2) A press on the picture in idle calls startPass, and a press in hold ejects and queues the next pass. (3) --copier-sheet-h is set on .copier__layout with (100cqw - 552px) * 1.25, so the minimum track sum stays inside the container (checked at 961px, 1024x1366 and 1440x700). (4) The DPR cap now uses (pointer: coarse) or innerWidth < 640. (5) resume() calls sound.drive(0) and sound.sleep() when hidden or offscreen, sleep() suspends the context after 260ms, and wake() and rouse() resume it.

issues.problem: In idle, a press on empty glass outside the picture still takes the pointer and drags the picture 1:1 (pose.x += dx no matter where the press landed), but it never starts a pass. The same gesture prints when it starts on the picture and prints nothing when it starts 10px outside it, which breaks 'every drag prints'.
issues.fix: In idle, drop the insideOriginal test so any press on the glass calls startPass(). Alternatively, when the press is outside the picture, return before pointers.set so empty glass is inert.

issues.problem: On a phone the sheet is almost full width and has touch-action: none. In hold, any touch on it (most often a swipe to scroll down to the panel) immediately ejects the held copy into the tray and starts a new pass. Visitors lose the vote frame without meaning to.
issues.fix: In hold, defer the eject for touch pointers: record the press, and call startPass only on pointerup with less than 8px of travel, or on the first move with |dx| greater than |dy| and more than 6px. Add `.copier-sheet[data-phase="hold"] { touch-action: pan-y; }` so vertical swipes scroll the page and fire pointercancel instead of ejecting.

issues.problem: The canvas reveal is a 900ms opacity fade over .copier-sheet__fallback::after, which still shows the static card. The GL card is already offset by the sway, by up to 44px, so the first second shows a ghosted double image.
issues.fix: Fade the fallback image out as the canvas comes in: `.copier-sheet[data-painted="true"] .copier-sheet__fallback::after { opacity: 0; transition: opacity 240ms var(--ease-hover); }`. Shorten the canvas fade to about 320ms, or reveal it with a clip-path wipe that follows the bar.

issues.problem: During every pass, including the autoplay pass that makes the vote frame, all seven source thumbnails switch to filter: grayscale(1) and the primary Copy button turns sunken grey. The first frame's chrome therefore reads as disabled, then everything pops back to colour about 1.2s later.
issues.fix: Drop the grayscale filter on `.copier-thumb:disabled` and keep only cursor: default. Better, let pickSource during a pass abort the pass, as loadSource already handles, and keep the thumbs enabled. For Copy during a pass, use aria-disabled with an unchanged look, not the sunken fill.

issues.problem: During a pinch or twist, a second finger that lands within 18px of the bar becomes the carriage instead of joining the gesture. Rotation stops and the scan jumps to that finger.
issues.fix: Allow carriage only when pointers.size === 0, by adding `pointers.size === 0 &&` to the carriage condition.

issues.problem: In the stacked layout the sheet is min(100% - 24px, 480px) wide at 4:5, so on a landscape phone (844x390) it is 600px tall in a 390px viewport. The bar and the bottom half of the copy are offscreen while you drag.
issues.fix: Cap the sheet by height too: `width: min(100% - 24px, 480px, (100dvh - 112px) * 0.8);`.

issues.problem: A double-click to recentre always runs its first pointerdown first. In hold that ejects the copy, and in idle on the picture it starts a pass. Recentring therefore also burns a copy.
issues.fix: Keep dblclick for recentring only in phase 'pass'. Otherwise rely on the 0 key and a re-click of the active thumbnail, both of which already recentre.

issues.problem: hover() calls host.getBoundingClientRect() on every pointermove, right after setNear() wrote --copier-near on the same host. That forces a style recalc and layout on every mouse move.
issues.fix: Cache rect in the ResizeObserver callback and in a passive scroll listener (capture) on window, and read the cached rect in hover, onWheel and onPointerDown.

issues.problem: Clicking Copy starts a pass and immediately sets disabled on the focused button, so keyboard focus drops to body mid-interaction. The preset and source radiogroups also lack arrow-key roving.
issues.fix: Use aria-disabled on the Copy and Copy the copy buttons and early-return in the handlers. Add ArrowLeft and ArrowRight roving with tabIndex -1 on the inactive radios.

issues.problem: `.copier-kbd` sets a raw `font-size: 0.86em` outside the type tokens. `.copier-originals__row` uses an off-grid `gap: 8px 6px`.
issues.fix: Give the kbd a text-ui-xs class (or the token) instead of the em size, and make the row gap 8px 4px.

recheck.wowGap: Make 'Copy the copy' compound on its own so the loop pays off. Holding Enter, or long-pressing Copy the copy, chains generations back to back at the 1.6s scan time. Each fed pass re-arms the scripted sway in the same phase (call the autoplay ledger logic with sway.ampTarget = SWAY_ROWS instead of a straight pass), the held sheet goes straight back onto the platen, and the Generation SlotNumber rolls every 1.6s. In about ten seconds Wagner melts from a gentle S into a deep toner ribbon, with contrast creep, fill-in and streak build-up stacking up, and releasing the key stops on the current generation in hold. Right now each extra generation needs a fresh manual sway, so most visitors will only ever see generation 1 or 2, and that compounding is the memorable part.

build.summary: A realistic session-booking card (Studio Two, Thu 15 Oct 2026, 14:00–17:00, £420.00, all tabular) whose signature field is a raw-WebGL2 paper-and-ink simulation. Water, suspended pigment, deposited pigment and a wet-history channel are held in RGBA32F or RGBA16F ping-pong targets, falling back to dithered RGBA8 and then to a Canvas2D stroke. Each stroke is stamped as tapered round-ended capsules, batched 64 per pass. Width comes from a broad nib held at 40°, combined with speed and Apple Pencil pressure. A pause grows a bead whose radius goes with the square root of dwell time, and dragging through wet ink smears it. Three 1/180s substeps per frame run a conservative 8-neighbour capillary flow, with fibre-weighted conductance and pinning over a fibre map drawn from strands. Evaporation is concentrated at the wet edge, so pigment is carried outward and dries into a real coffee ring. A 4-tap supersampled display adds granulation, a damp tide line and a wet gloss lit from the water height, which fades as the ink dries in about 2–3s. On load a hand-written 'Herb' (Catmull-Rom path, slower on tight curves, beads at each stroke end) writes itself in 2.2s. 'Sign and book' unlocks once enough ink is down. It slides a blotter over the field, presses it, and reads back a feathered offprint of whatever is still wet. The blotter flips with scaleX to show that offprint mirrored, then blurs away. The button morphs from 'Blotting' to 'Booked' with a pop, and the timestamp rolls in on SlotNumber. A hand-rolled panel has three presets (Fountain, Felt tip, Brush), four real ink colours and Absorbency and Drying sliders with rolling readouts. On phones the panel collapses into a disclosure.
build.wowMoment: Hold the pen still at the end of a stroke. A glossy bead swells under the nib and wicks out into the paper fibres. As it dries over about three seconds the gloss goes matte and the pigment migrates into a darker rim. Then press 'Sign and book': the blotter lifts a mirrored, feathered copy of exactly the ink that was still wet.
build.knownIssues: The piece has never been viewed in a browser, per the hard rules. To compensate, the physics, nib model and display shading were ported to a CPU script in the scratchpad and the intro and a 1s pause were rendered to PNG for all three presets. Those renders show thick/thin contrast, beads at the stroke ends, a coffee ring, granulation and wet gloss. Every shader also compiles under glslc with an OpenGL target. The only glslc error is an overlapping uniform location on the array uniforms in the stamp shader, and that came from my extraction script's layout rewriting, not from the shader. Still unverified on a real GPU: the exact colours and timing, the gloss strength, and how the blotter flip feels. The RGBA8 fallback relies on stochastic dithering, so it will look noisier. A WebGL context loss clears the ink and gives no new 'Sign and book' unlock until the person signs again. On a resize of more than 1.5×, an untouched intro signature is replayed rather than stretched; ink the person drew is rescaled instead.

critique.firstFrame: Server HTML is a quiet light page. It has the "Wet ink" title, then a white booking card that blurs and rises in: Studio Two, Thu 15 Oct 2026 (that date is a Thursday), 14:00–17:00, 3 hours, £140 per hour, total £420.00, all in tabular numerals. Below that sits a white signature field with a 1px subtle border, a line-strong baseline at 66% height and an "x", and on the right the Pen and ink panel. On mount the WebGL canvas fades in from blur over 900ms. At 560ms a paced cursive "Herb" starts writing, slower at turns, with broad-nib thick and thin strokes. The ink goes down dark, small pools form at the end of the H stem (120ms hold) and the b tail (300ms hold), and the line dries slightly darker than it went down because deposit counts 1.0 and suspended pigment counts 0.8. It ends with a fast underline flick that has no hold. "Sign and book" turns on when the intro finishes. Weak points: the field is flat #fff, exactly like the card, so it reads as an ordinary input until ink lands. The intro never shows the brief's wow moment (a long hold that swells, feathers and dries into a ring), because the last stroke is a flick. It is a strong, physical first frame, not yet a jaw-drop.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate wet-ink: PASS (lint, comments, type system, tokens). 2. compile-check wet-ink: PASS (10 modules). 3. glsl-check: all 6 shaders ok (the quad vertex plus the stamp, step, lift, display and offprint fragments). They are plain strings with no ${} interpolation, so the check is meaningful. Things I checked by reading the code: every uniform is set, array uniforms resolve through "[0]", no feedback loops (each pass samples only the read target on unit 0), 64 + 64 vec4 uniforms is under the WebGL2 minimum of 224, and the float → half → RGBA8 → Canvas2D fallback chain is complete. Neighbour flux is a symmetric pair gather (shared fibre and pin terms), so water and pigment are conserved. Half-float stochastic-rounding dither keeps tiny evaporation steps from rounding to zero. Context loss and restore are handled, and so are StrictMode double-mount, timer cleanup on unmount, hidden-tab and offscreen pause with clock shifting, the DPR cap of 2 (1.5 on narrow screens) with a governor, and idle stop. No SSR window access.

issues.problem: The drying clock is wall time (wetHold = max(5000, 3600/dry + 1600)), not tied to how much water is left. A bead held for 1–3s reaches the 2.0 water cap. Interior evaporation is about 0.08 + 0.2w per second, which takes ~9s from 2.0 even before spreading, so the rAF loop stops while the pool is still wet. That freezes the gloss, the damp paper tone and the suspended pigment mid-dry, and the coffee ring never finishes. This is exactly the brief's wow moment. At the 0.4 drying setting it is worse (~10s hold against ~20s of drying). It only starts again on the next stamp or slider change.
issues.fix: Make 'busy' depend on actual water. Every ~20 frames, render a 1/8-res max-reduction of state.r into a tiny RGBA8 target and readPixels it asynchronously through a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER plus gl.fenceSync. Keep running until max water < 0.004, with a 30s safety cap. A cheaper version: track the deepest bead water stamped since the last dry on the CPU, and set wetUntil = now + (5·ln((w+0.4)/0.4) + 1.5)/dry seconds.

issues.problem: The intro ends on a fast underline flick (pace 1.9, hold 0). The only pools are 120ms and 300ms holds mid-signature, so the first frame never shows what the brief is selling: a bead swelling, wicking out along fibres, then drying with a dark rim.
issues.fix: Give the last stroke a ~700ms hold (or move the 300ms hold to 700ms on the b tail and drop the underline). Shave the hold time off the other strokes so SIGNATURE_MS still lands near 2.2s plus the hold. Together with the drying fix above, the ring then visibly forms 2–4s after load.

issues.problem: Bead radius grows as sqrt(still) with no cap, and keeps getting 4 water per second up to 2.0. With pin 0.12, 2.0 water spreads until the front is about 0.12 deep, so a 2–3s hold can flood a blot 50–100px across instead of 'a few hairs wick out'. That reads as a spill, not feathering.
issues.fix: Clamp the bead to r + bead·sqrt(min(still, 1.2)). Taper the water rate after ~0.8s (pool·dt·exp(-still)). In the step shader, raise pinning in proportion to 1 − fibre so spreading follows the strands and stalls on the gaps between them.

issues.problem: Picking an ink chip tweens the uniform uInk, which recolours the ink already on the page, dried strokes included. It behaves like a theme switch, not an ink, and breaks the physical illusion the piece is built on.
issues.fix: Only the next ink should change. The cheap way: on an ink change, if anything is on the page, run the 520ms clear sweep and replay the intro in the new ink. The faithful way: add a second pigment channel pair (or a hue texture written by the stamp pass) so each stroke keeps its own colour.

issues.problem: Dry paper renders as exactly uPaper = #fff with no fibre tone. The brief's '0.03 grain' is missing, so the field looks like a blank input until ink lands, and the paper material that Herb's taste loves is invisible in the first frame.
issues.fix: Add a constant 0.012 + 0.018·fibre.r (with the existing 0.5 hash mix) to paperShade everywhere, not only under tide or damp. Fade it in with the 900ms canvas reveal so the white-to-paper change reads as part of the entrance.

issues.problem: MAX_SUBSTEPS = 4 at SUBSTEP 1/180 covers only 22ms per frame. At 30–40fps (iOS Low Power Mode, a throttled iframe) the accumulator is zeroed every frame and the sim runs in slow motion while the wall-clock drying hold keeps counting. That makes the freeze above more likely on phones.
issues.fix: Let substeps scale to cover dt up to 50ms (MAX_SUBSTEPS = 9). Alternatively, when steps hit the cap, pass the leftover time as a larger uDt to the last step (diffusion weights don't use dt, so that is safe).

issues.problem: The intro starts at 560ms, while the canvas is still at ~80% opacity with ~1px of blur (900ms reveal) and the card is finishing its blur-in. The slow launch of the H stem happens half-hidden, so the first impression is the middle of a stroke.
issues.fix: Set INTRO_DELAY_MS to about 880ms, or start the intro from the canvas transitionend or animationend of wi-card-in, so the pen touches down on fully revealed paper.

issues.problem: penStill overwrites pen.t with the rAF timestamp, which can be later than the next pointer event's timeStamp. The first move out of a pool then gets elapsed clamped to 0.5ms, the speed spikes and the stroke snaps thin, giving a visible notch where you leave a puddle.
issues.fix: Keep a separate pen.stillSince for the hold, leave pen.t as the last event time, and compute elapsed from event timestamps only.

issues.problem: wi-pop runs keyframes 0.96 → 1.04 → 1 with --ease-overshoot on each segment, so it overshoots twice (past 1.04, then under 1), which is a bounce. It also starts from 0.96 while the booking phase holds 0.98, so there is a 2% snap at the moment of the label morph.
issues.fix: Use a plain ease-out-quint curve for the keyframes (they already encode the overshoot). Either start the keyframe at 0.98, or drop the booking-phase scale.

issues.problem: paintFibres runs on the main thread at mount and on every resize past 6%. It draws ~2,500 canvas strokes, calls getImageData and runs a per-pixel JS loop over ~130k pixels, roughly 20–50ms on a phone, and it lands right in the middle of the card entrance animation.
issues.fix: Generate the fibre map in a one-off GPU pass (a strand hash plus anisotropic noise in a fragment shader into the RGBA8 fibre texture). Or cache the CPU result keyed by size and defer it with requestIdleCallback until after the entrance.

issues.problem: Reduced motion still renders the wet sheen and gloss (uSheen is always 1) on strokes the user draws, and on any pool the instant 760-step pre-dry didn't finish. The brief says no sheen under reduced motion.
issues.fix: Set renderSettings.sheen = this.reducedMotion ? 0 : 1, and give the reduced-motion intro enough pre-dry steps (about 1600) to reach zero water.

issues.problem: lock(false) after 'New booking' never shows the nib again. With cursor: none on the field, a mouse already resting over the field after the reset has no cursor at all until it leaves and comes back.
issues.fix: In lock(false), if the surface :hover matches and finePointer is true, set nib data-visible to true.

critique.wowGap: Make the intro end on the hero moment and let it finish. Give the final stroke a ~700ms nib hold so a bead swells and wicks out along the fibres. Then keep the sim running until the measured maximum water reaches zero, using an async 1/8-res max-reduction readback, instead of stopping on the 5s wall clock. Within 4 seconds of load the visitor would then see a live puddle feather out and dry into a dark coffee ring with the sheen fading, all before touching anything. Right now the intro ends on a flick, and any long hold freezes half-wet.

changes: SignaturePad.js: drying now follows measured water instead of a wall clock. Every 20 frames it reads back an async 1/8-res max of the water and keeps the loop running until max water is below threshold, with a 30s safety cap. A stamp-generation counter ignores stale readbacks, and the 600ms minimum hold and safety deadline both shift correctly across pauses.

InkSim.js + wetInkShader.js: new REDUCE_FRAGMENT. It takes the 8x8 max of water by texelFetch, sqrt-encodes it into an RGBA8 target and reads it back through readPixels into a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER with fenceSync/clientWaitSync/getBufferSubData. It is rebuilt on resize and disposed in destroy.

signaturePath.js: dropped the underline flick. The b tail is now the last stroke with a 700ms nib hold (H stem 80ms), SIGNATURE_MS is 2300 and BOX is trimmed to the new extent. The bead swells at about 2.5s after mount and then dries live into its ring.
SignaturePad.js: the bead radius stops growing at 1.2s of hold and its water rate tapers by exp(-still). The reduced-motion bead uses the same capped model.
wetInkShader.js STEP: pinning is now uPin*(0.55+2.6*(1-fibre)^2), so spreading stalls on the gaps between fibres and wicks along strands.

Ink colour is now per stroke: a TINT_FRAGMENT pass, run per stamp batch, writes the ink colour into a ping-pong RGBA8 tint map (core plus halo on bare paper). Display and offprint read it, so picking a chip only changes the next ink. Tints are cleared on clear, blitted on resize and disposed. The uInk tween is removed. FlatInk stores a colour per segment.
Paper tone: constant 0.012 + 0.018*fibre*(grain mix) on all paper, and PAPER_HEX is a faint warm #fdfbf7. The field turns from white card to fibred paper as part of the 900ms canvas reveal.

Perf: MAX_SUBSTEPS is 9 (covers a 50ms dt) and the leftover is clamped rather than zeroed. The CPU paintFibres (canvas strokes, getImageData, per-pixel loop) is replaced by a one-off GPU FIBRE_FRAGMENT pass: integer-hashed bent strands at about the same density with a slight horizontal bias, plus anisotropic value-noise haze and per-pixel grain, rendered into an RGBA8 target (highp int).
INTRO_DELAY_MS is 920, so the pen touches down on fully revealed paper.
penStill no longer overwrites pen.t. The first move out of a pool caps its dwell at 30ms and computes speed from event timestamps only, so there is no notch when you leave a puddle.
wet-ink.css: wi-pop keyframes now run 0.98 -> 1.04 -> 1 on --ease-out-quint (no double overshoot, no 2% snap). The unused --wi-ease-pop is removed.
Reduced motion: sheen is 0, the intro pre-dries for 1600 steps, and the loop then lets the probe confirm the ink is fully dry.
lock(false): re-shows the nib when a fine pointer is already hovering over the field (only once its position is known).
experiment.json: description rewritten around the self-signing hold and coffee ring. Title Wet ink, tags, intent and status candidate are kept, and building is false.
polish.remaining: I didn't run anything in a browser, as instructed. Every change is checked only by hand-tracing and by the three checks (lab-gate PASS, compile PASS, GLSL all ok), so these need an eye in a real browser: (1) how big the 700ms intro bead ends up with the new fibre pinning, which should be a feathered blot of roughly 20-30px and not a spill (tune nib.pool/bead or the 2.6 pinning factor if it is too big); (2) whether the GPU fibre texture looks like the old CPU one; (3) the 8-bit readback threshold. Tracing shows the sim's 0.004 cutoff encodes to byte 11, and DRY_READING is 0.002 so that byte still counts as wet. The tint halo is 6 + 3x the nib radius in sim pixels, so ink that feathers further than that from a stroke falls back to the current ink colour. That only shows if you change ink while that ink is still wet.

recheck.firstFrame: The header rises, then a cream booking card blurs in (Session booking, Studio Two · Mix room, No. 2481, Thu 15 Oct 2026, 14:00–17:00, 3 hours, £140 per hour, Total £420.00, all tabular; Thu 15 Oct 2026 really is a Thursday and 3 × 140 = 420). Below it is a signature field with a strong 1px baseline at 66% and an 'x'. The paper canvas fades in from blur over 900ms with visible fibre strands. At 920ms an iron-gall 'Herb' writes itself. The speed profile is natural: around 1.15 px/ms on the straights, dropping to 0.3–0.5 at turns. The broad nib gives real thick-thin contrast and there is a small 80ms pool at the foot of the H. The b's exit stroke stops at about (370,111) and holds for 700ms, from t≈2.5s to 3.2s. A bead swells to about 10px radius, about 400 px²·units of water spreads into a pale puddle roughly 35–45px across, and it feathers out along the fibre strands. Then 'Sign and book' enables. Because the water probe now keeps the sim alive until it is actually dry, the puddle finishes drying over the next ~2–4s with a darker rim, a tide line and the damp paper tone fading. The hero moment now plays out by itself, before any touch, and finishes. Two weaker spots: no pen is visible while the ink writes itself, and the strokes dry within ~0.5s, so only the final pool reads as wet.
recheck.checks: lab-gate wet-ink: PASS. lab-compile-check wet-ink: PASS (10 modules). lab-glsl-check src/app/lab/wet-ink: all 9 shader literals ok (QUAD_VERTEX:3, STAMP:9, STEP:69, LIFT:154, DISPLAY:187, OFFPRINT:263, TINT:305, REDUCE:347, FIBRE:366). Both previous findings are fixed and verified. (1) Drying is now measured, not wall-clock: every 20 frames a 1/8-res max-reduction is read back asynchronously through a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER and fenceSync; a stamp-generation guard throws away stale reads; the sim runs until max water < 0.002, with a 30s safety cap and pause shifting (SignaturePad.js 347-372, InkSim.js 220-276). (2) The last stroke now holds for 700ms (signaturePath.js 15) and SIGNATURE_MS is 2300; I measured events at down@0, up@283, down@393, last move@1600, up@2300.

issues.problem: frame() calls paint() and then sampleGovernor(). When the governor steps, applyDisplaySize changes canvas.width/height, which clears the drawing buffer after the frame has already been drawn. With alpha:false, the composited frame is a fully black signature field. On slow devices the governor steps every 40+ frames, so the field visibly flashes black. If the step lands on the last busy frame, the field stays black until the next wake. measure() (line 180-191) has the same hole: when a rAF is already pending it skips paint(), so resizing the window while ink is wet flashes black for one frame.
issues.fix: Call this.sampleGovernor(dt) before this.paint() in frame(). In measure(), call this.paint() unconditionally after applyDisplaySize() instead of only when !this.raf. A render is cheap, and any canvas resize must be followed by a draw in the same task.

issues.problem: Strokes dry in about 0.3–0.6s. Stroke water is about 0.12–0.18, almost every stroke pixel has a dry neighbour, so rim = 1. Evaporation is then about 1.1·0.36 + 0.1 ≈ 0.5/s, and the stroke erodes inward in roughly half a second. The wet look (30% darker ink, damp halo, gloss at water 0.12 only ~0.4 strength) therefore lasts a blink on lines. The brief says the sheen fades over about 3.5s and must stay visible for 2–3s. 'Drag through still-wet ink to smear' only works inside pools, because smear carry needs behind.r > 0.02 and the line is already dry.
issues.fix: Gate the rim term on body depth so only pools build coffee rings: evaporation = uDt*uDry*(0.05 + 0.2*water + 1.1*rim*smoothstep(0.18, 0.5, highest)). Raise the fountain preset's nib.base from 0.12 to about 0.16. Thin lines then stay wet about 1.5–2.5s, the smear works along a fresh stroke, and pools keep their fast rim and dark ring. Check the felt preset (dry 1.4) still reads as quick-drying.

issues.problem: During the intro the ink writes itself with no pen. The wi-nib dot only follows a real pointer, so the 700ms hold reads as ink growing by itself rather than 'the pen rests and the ink swells'.
issues.fix: In feedIntro, call this.moveNib({x: event.x, y: event.y}) for each event and set nib data-visible='true' / data-down='true' while the intro is active. On the final 'up', set data-down='false'. After 200ms, hide the nib unless a real fine pointer is hovering. The existing scale(0.55) press state then shows the pen pressing during the bead.

issues.problem: Nib radii (0.4–3px) and the bead growth (9px) are absolute CSS pixels, but the intro signature scales with the field. On a 311×130 phone field the signature scale is 0.295, so the x-height is about 27px. The final bead still grows to about 10px radius and spreads into a puddle about 40px across, a blot bigger than the letters. Strokes are also heavy for the scale.
issues.fix: Have buildSignature return its scale. While the intro plays, multiply nib.min/max/bead by clamp(scale/0.53, 0.6, 1) (0.53 is the desktop scale). Scale nib.pool by the square of that factor, so the bead's water volume scales with its area.

issues.problem: The reduced-motion intro runs INSTANT_DRY_STEPS = 1600 full-resolution step passes synchronously in one task. Each pass makes about 18 fetches per pixel; at 560×233 RGBA32F that is about 3.8G texel fetches. That causes a 100–300ms+ hitch on load on integrated or mobile GPUs, for exactly the users who asked for calm.
issues.fix: Run the instant dry with a larger effective dt: about 200 steps of SUBSTEP·8 with uAbsorb scaled by 1/8, so flow stays stable. Or spread the 1600 steps over the first ~10 frames, 160 per frame, with the canvas still behind its 900ms fade-in.

issues.problem: The first touch after the intro draws straight over Herb's 'Herb' signature. The header copy invites drawing but never mentions Clear, so most visitors' first stroke lands on top of the autograph and the result looks messy.
issues.fix: If !this.userInk and this.inkLength > 0 when the pointer goes down, lift the intro ink first. Run a fast 280ms right-to-left lift sweep, or this.sim.lift(4, 0.01, CLEARED) under a 160ms opacity dip, before the first stamp. Or change the header to say 'Clear to sign it yourself'.

issues.problem: The canvas reveal uses a raw cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1) and a raw 900ms, and several transitions use raw ms values (440, 140, 180, 640, 520) where every other easing in the file uses a house token. It is not one house easing.
issues.fix: Use var(--ease-entrance) for the canvas reveal. Use the duration tokens that exist (--duration-800 for the reveal, --duration-400/--duration-500 for the blotter legs) where the timing allows, and keep raw values only where they are tied to the BLOT_STEPS timers.

recheck.wowGap: Make the wet state impossible to miss on the whole signature, not only the final pool. Keep shallow strokes wet for 1.5–2.5s by gating rim evaporation on depth (rim × smoothstep(0.18, 0.5, highest)). Then give the display a real meniscus glint: take the normal from a 5-tap-blurred water height scaled ×10, use pow(…, 40) × 0.5 white, and gate it with smoothstep(0.03, 0.2, water). As the pen writes 'Herb', a glossy dark line then trails behind it and dulls to matte from the H forward. The final bead catches a crisp highlight that shrinks as the puddle flattens, and goes out as the coffee ring darkens in.

changes: SignaturePad.frame: sampleGovernor now runs before paint, so a governor canvas resize can no longer leave a black field; measure() always paints after applyDisplaySize (the jump/introPending branches fall through instead of returning)

wetInkShader STEP: evaporation = uDt*uDry*(0.05 + 0.2*water + 1.1*rim*smoothstep(0.18, 0.5, highest)), so only pools build fast rims and coffee rings while shallow strokes stay wet for about 1.5-2.5s and can be smeared

wetInkParams: fountain base 0.12 to 0.16, with concentration 4.2 to 3.2 and poolConcentration 0.09 to 0.118 so pigment per stroke and per pool stays the same; felt base 0.08 (concentration 6.25, poolConcentration 0.12) and dry 1.4 to 1.8 so felt still dries in about 0.75s; SignaturePad defaults match

wetInkShader DISPLAY: the old pow-14 gloss is replaced by a meniscus glint. The normal comes from a 5-tap-blurred water height scaled x10, the glint is pow(dot(n, halfway), 40) x 0.5 white, gated by smoothstep(0.03, 0.2, water) and uSheen, and sits inside a dynamic branch with textureLod so dry pixels skip the extra 20 fetches. Fresh strokes now trail a glossy line that dulls from the H forward, and the bead's crisp highlight shrinks as the puddle flattens

Intro pen: feedIntro moves the wi-nib dot to the latest event each frame and sets data-visible and data-down on each stroke's down and up, so the 700ms hold shows the pen pressed. After the final up the dot lingers 200ms, then hides, or snaps back to a hovering fine pointer. Real pointer moves don't fight the intro dot
Mobile scale: buildSignature returns its scale. During the intro, nib radii and bead grow by clamp(scale/0.53, 0.6, 1) and pool volume by that factor squared, reset when the intro ends
Reduced motion: the 1600 instant-dry steps now run 160 per frame across 10 frames instead of in one synchronous task; the governor ignores those frames

First touch after the intro: if no user ink exists yet, the autograph is drawn into a multiply-blended ghost canvas that fades, blurs and lifts away over 300ms while the sim clears underneath, and 'Sign and book' resets to wait for the user's own signature

Pre-existing fix: a tap, Clear or Enter before the 920ms intro delay no longer leaves the intro timer armed (it used to write Herb over the user's ink later), and phase still leaves 'intro', so 'Sign and book' can enable

wet-ink.css: canvas reveal now uses var(--duration-800) var(--ease-entrance), and the other transitions and animations use --duration-* tokens; only the 180ms blotter turn, which is tied to BLOT_STEPS, and the stagger delays stay raw. New .wi-ghost styles have a reduced-motion opacity-only variant
experiment.json: description refreshed to mention the glossy wet strokes; building false, status candidate
polish2.remaining: Not verified in a browser (per the rules). These visual values were reasoned out but are untuned: glint strength on thin strokes (about 0.15 white on upper-left edges at the x5 per-texel slope), how much extra fibre feathering the longer-wet strokes get, and how the ghost lift looks. If stroke glints read as outlines, lower the 5.0 slope factor in DISPLAY_FRAGMENT; if the bead highlight is too faint, raise it toward 7.

build.summary: A sheet of fibre paper in a tray of developer, run by a shallow-water simulation on the GPU (virtual-pipe model, 144×180 grid, raw WebGL2 ping-pong targets). Each sheet gets slightly uneven paper, the tilt follows a spring, and dragging pushes water under the pointer. Wherever the liquid has been, a development-time value builds up, faster where it is agitated, and keeps going briefly after the water leaves. The print shader turns that into silver density: shadows come up first, highlights fill in slowly, and whites fog if left too long. The water shows as a faint amber tint, refraction, glints and a crisp edge line, and every print has a white easel border. Pressing anywhere tips the tray so the developer runs to your finger; flicks send big waves, arrow keys tip and Space rocks. Next sheet slides the print onto a drying line of thumbnails while a fresh sheet slides in, and a column of negatives (John, Paul, George, 12 T206 card scans, recent covers) picks the source. A left panel holds 4 presets and 5 sliders with rolling readouts; the timer rolls and a status changes from Developing to Fogging.
build.wowMoment: The first frame was pre-simulated for 1.2s: a developer wave is mid-crossing from the bottom right toward the top left, with a bright edge line and glints. John's hair, glasses and beard are already warm black where it has washed, and a clean diagonal leaves the top-right of the sheet paper white. Then it sloshes back into a pool at the bottom, and holding anywhere makes the liquid run toward your finger.
build.knownIssues: Never run in a browser (no browser allowed). The simulation and display maths were ported to a Node/sharp prototype that rendered the opening frames to PNG for tuning; the shaders passed the GLSL syntax check and a manual type review but were never compiled by a real WebGL driver. A full-tilt flick was stable in the CPU prototype with no water lost, but has not been seen on a GPU. If no float render target is available, the page shows a static greyscale still with a 'needs WebGL2' note; the brief's 8-bit fallback simulation is not built. Under reduced motion the water is hidden but still drives development, rather than the brief's separate 600ms reveal. Clicking a negative throws away the current sheet; it only goes on the drying line if it developed for at least 1s. Spotify covers need a CORS-enabled image host; if one fails to load, the current sheet stays.

critique.firstFrame: The plate shows a paper-white placeholder until the chunk and john.webp have loaded and decoded. Then 72 synchronous pre-sim steps run and the canvas fades in over 900ms. The water starts as a resting pool along the bottom 17% of the sheet. The intro lean (-0.1, 0.13) throws it up and to the left, so by the reveal the bottom and left of the face are developed. A warm amber sheet of developer with a crisp rim and lip highlight is still travelling, then slides back into the bottom pool about 0.4s later. The builder's own prototype render (scratchpad/develop/g1.png and strip.png) shows roughly 80% of John's face already finished at reveal, midtones included. Only a wedge at the top right is still white. It looks photographic and the liquid reads as liquid, not as a wipe mask, which is good. But the brief's moment ("only the shadows exist, the rest is white paper with a latent grey") has mostly been spent before the visitor touches it. Upscaling 200px source to about 500 CSS px with B-spline sampling gives a soft but acceptable photographic look.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate develop: PASS. 2. compile-check develop: PASS (9 modules). 3. glsl-check src/app/lab/develop: all 9 shaders ok (FULLSCREEN_VERTEX, COCKLE, RESET, FLUX, HEIGHT, DEVELOP, FIELD, STATS, PRINT). They are plain #version 300 es strings with precision declared, no interpolation, and every sampler bound. The API audit is clean. It uses raw WebGL2 (no R3F). EXT_color_buffer_float has a fallback to half float. Outflow is clamped and h is kept >= 0. At the CFL limit, dt = 1/480 with c of at most about 135 cells/s gives a Courant number of about 0.28. The accumulator is ping-ponged rather than blended. Pointer capture uses pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture with no double-fire. The DeviceOrientation permission is requested inside the click handler. crossOrigin is set before src. ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, visibility and context-loss handling are all in place. Cleanup is thorough and calls loseContext. There is no SSR window access outside effects or guards.

issues.problem: The first frame gives away the reveal. The 1.2s pre-sim starts with the bottom pool already wet and throws a full-sheet wave, and the develop rate (0.3 + 0.9 × exposure) is only about 1.6× faster for blacks than for midtones. So at reveal most of the face, midtones included, is already developed (see the builder's g1.png). The visitor's first rock only fills a corner, which kills 'one tilt and a face appears only where the wave touched it'.
issues.fix: Shorten PRESIM_SECONDS to about 0.6 and use a smaller intro lean (about 0.08), so the front stops near the diagonal. In PRINT_FRAGMENT, make development strongly shadows-first: progress = 1 - exp(-DEVELOP_K * effectiveTime * (0.08 + 1.1 * pow(exposure, 1.8))). Then the first frame holds only eyes, brows, hair and beard in warm black with paper-white skin, and the second rock visibly breathes the midtones in.

issues.problem: Next sheet and chip picks call api.retire(), which calls freshSheet(), before the next image has loaded. The new white sheet keeps the old imageTexture, and the always-wet bottom pool starts developing the previous portrait. When an uncached source arrives (a 150KB card, a remote cover), setImage swaps the texture under the already-developed strip, and the region pops from one face to another. Nothing preloads upcoming sources.
issues.fix: In retireTo, call `loadSource(sources[nextIndex]).then(() => api.retire())` (or pass the loaded result into retire so freshSheet calls engine.setImage before resetSheet). Also warm the cache for the next two sources after reveal with loadSource(sources[i+1]). Alternatively, have resetSheet set a pending flag that holds develope() until setImage lands.

issues.problem: IDLE_STOP_MS is 45000, so after every interaction a rAF loop runs at display rate for 45s. It renders full-resolution at 12fps and calls readPixels every 0.4s. The brief asked for about 6s, because the /taste preload iframe and the experiments index keep this alive.
issues.fix: Set IDLE_STOP_MS to about 8000. In the !moving branch, drop rAF and schedule the 12fps develop/render with setTimeout(frame, 83), so the display isn't woken every vsync.

issues.problem: readStats() calls gl.readPixels synchronously every 0.4s, straight after the frame's 16 sim passes and the full-resolution PRINT draw (up to 2.5M pixels × 16 fetches). That forces a CPU-GPU sync each time, which on phones and integrated GPUs shows up as a periodic hitch about 2.5 times a second while dragging.
issues.fix: Use an async readback. Render the STATS pass, readPixels into a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER, then gl.fenceSync. On later frames, poll clientWaitSync(fence, 0, 0) and only call getBufferSubData once it is signalled. Because the timer only needs whole seconds, a frame or two of latency is invisible.

issues.problem: The print-line slide uses the wrong step. Vertical rows are 72 + 8 = 80px, but the animation starts at -90px. Horizontal (phone) items are 56 + 8 = 64px, but it starts at -80px. Existing thumbnails jump 10px or 16px on the first frame of every new print.
issues.fix: Measure the step instead of hard-coding it. Read list.firstElementChild.nextElementSibling's offsetTop or offsetLeft minus the first child's (or use 80 vertical and 64 horizontal), and animate from exactly that distance.

issues.problem: The negative strip puts all 23 full-size sources in as CSS background images (12 T206 cards at 660×1232, about 150KB each, plus covers) just to show 40×52 thumbs. That is about 2MB downloaded and decoded on load, competing with the main portrait.
issues.fix: Render each negative with next/image (sizes='40px', loading='lazy') inside the button, or generate 80px thumbs. Keep the CSS invert/grayscale filter on the img element.

issues.problem: loadSource failures are swallowed with .catch(() => undefined). If the very first source fails (a 404, or a cover host without CORS), the plate stays blank paper forever with no message. A failed later source silently keeps the old image.
issues.fix: On rejection, call onFailure('source') and have DevelopExperience advance to the next source index (or drop that source from the list). Only show the WebGL2 failure message for engine failures.

issues.problem: The static fallback .develop-still uses `inset: 5.5% 5.5% 4.4%`. Inset percentages for top and bottom resolve against height, so the correct border is 4.4% vertical and 5.5% horizontal. As written, the fallback image sits 1.1% high and does not match the WebGL print border.
issues.fix: Use `inset: 4.4% 5.5%`.

issues.problem: Thumbnails are full-resolution JPEG blobs (canvas.width × canvas.height, up to about 1400×1760) that are shown at 56×72. Blob URLs pushed out by slice(0, MAX_PRINTS) are never revoked until unmount.
issues.fix: Keep the full-size blob only for download. Draw a separate 112×144 thumbnail canvas for the background image. When slicing past MAX_PRINTS, revoke the dropped prints' URLs and remove them from urlsRef.

issues.problem: Clicking a print in the session line downloads a file straight away, with no visual response. As the only interaction on the drying line it is surprising and lacks press feedback.
issues.fix: Have a click lift the print, for example a 200ms scale to 1.06 with a ring. Keep the download on a second click, or put a small 'Save' action on hover/focus with the label as the title.

issues.problem: The dashed empty placeholder in the print line is a generic empty-state detail that reads as unfinished chrome beside a quiet Swiss layout.
issues.fix: Remove the dashed placeholder and let the rail stay empty until the first print lands. If a cue is needed, use a 1px var(--color-line-subtle) hairline the height of one thumb.

issues.problem: On devices with only EXT_color_buffer_half_float, development time accumulates in RGBA16F. Past T≈32s each frame's 0.0167s increment rounds up to the 0.031 ulp, and past T≈64s it rounds to 0. Fog then speeds up and then freezes, and the timer stalls.
issues.fix: On the half-float path, accumulate a frame's develop time in JS and run the develop pass at most every 0.1s with dt ≥ 0.1. Or store time divided by 8 in the half-float target and scale it back up in PRINT and STATS.

issues.problem: Under reduced motion the shallow-water sim still runs with the water invisible, so blotches of development crawl across the sheet in the shape of an unseen wave. The brief asked for a direct 600ms develop under the tilt.
issues.fix: When reduced, skip simulate(). On drag, arrow key or tap, write a soft disc or half-plane wet mask toward the lean direction into the height target via the RESET program, fading in over 600ms, so development happens in place without a moving wave.

critique.wowGap: Give the first touch back to the visitor. Make the pre-sim stop at a clean diagonal front (about 0.6s, smaller intro lean) and make development steeply shadows-first, with the rate scaled by pow(exposure, 1.8). Then the first frame shows only John's eyes, glasses, brows and beard in warm black on white paper, with the live meniscus parked on the diagonal. The first hold-and-drag visibly washes the skin and midtones in under the finger, which is exactly the brief's 'face appears only where the wave touched it' moment.

changes: developShader.js PRINT_FRAGMENT: development is now steeply shadows-first, with progress = 1 - exp(-1.2 * T * (0.08 + 1.1 * pow(exposure, 1.8))). Blacks develop about 3x faster than midtones and about 8x faster than skin highlights.

DevelopStage.jsx intro: I replaced the single hard lean with a scripted INTRO_STEPS sequence. It holds level for 0.1s, throws at (-0.11, 0.12) until 0.7s, then settles at a mild (-0.03, -0.03). The pre-sim is 0.95s and the live script resumes at that offset. I checked this in my CPU prototype (scratchpad/develop/proto3.mjs, c1-c4.png, d1-d3.png). The reveal frame shows John's hair, glasses, brows and beard in warm black on white paper, cut by a clean diagonal from upper left to lower right, with the meniscus parked on it. The skin stays white after the water drains, and later rocks visibly bring the midtones in.

Deviation from the reviewer's numbers: the suggested 0.6s pre-sim with a 0.08 lean only moved water out of the bottom pool. Its reveal showed nothing but the beard strip (n_*.png), so I used 0.95s with an early throw that relaxes to a parked lean.

Next sheet and chip picks: DevelopExperience now loads the next source first, then calls api.retire(loaded). retire, through freshSheet, calls engine.setImage before resetSheet, so a new sheet can never develop the previous portrait. setImage skips a duplicate upload of the same loaded object, and overlapping requests are guarded by a request token.

Sources are tracked by id instead of index. Load failures, including on the first source, now report onFailure('source', id). The failed source is dropped from the strip and the plate falls through to the next one; Next sheet keeps trying the following sources. The WebGL2 message is shown only for engine failures.
Cache warming: after each reveal or fresh sheet (onReady, after 900ms) the next two sources are preloaded, and hovering or focusing a negative also preloads it (warmSource in developSources.js).

Loop: IDLE_STOP_MS drops from 45000 to 8000. When nothing is moving, development and rendering run on setTimeout at 83ms (about 12fps) using the real elapsed time, so the display is no longer woken every vsync. Any input cancels the timer and switches back to requestAnimationFrame.

developEngine.js stats are now read asynchronously. The stats pass is read into a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER, guarded by fenceSync and polled with clientWaitSync(fence, 0, 0) each frame, then copied out with getBufferSubData. resetSheet discards any pending fence, and the loop waits for one last settled stat before going idle.

Half-float time accumulation: DEVELOP_FRAGMENT adds each frame's time to a pending channel (dev.a) and folds it into dev.r per cell once it reaches max(0.05, T/256). FIELD and STATS read r + a. This keeps the rounding error bounded on RGBA16F, so fog no longer speeds up and then freezes, and the timer no longer stalls.

Reduced motion: a new STILL_FRAGMENT and engine.settle() replace the water simulation. They write the rest pool plus a soft half-plane of developer toward the lean into the height target, eased in over about 600ms (time constant 0.2s), with flux cleared and the paddle off. Drag, arrow keys, taps, the rock and the pre-sim now develop in place with no unseen crawling wave.

Thumbnails: retire returns a full-size JPEG for downloading and a separate 112x140 thumbnail for the rail. Prints pushed past MAX_PRINTS have both URLs revoked, and prints that are not kept are revoked straight away.
DevelopBench.jsx print line: the slide now measures the real step between the first two items (offsetTop or offsetLeft) instead of the hard-coded 90px or 80px.
Print line clicks: the first click lifts the print (scale 1.06 over 200ms with a ring), and a second click saves it. Escape or blur drops the lift, and the label and title change to say Save.
The dashed empty placeholder is gone from the JSX and the CSS.

Negatives: each one now renders through next/image (fill, sizes 40px, lazy) inside the button, with the invert and grayscale filter moved onto the img. This replaces about 2MB of full-size CSS background images.
develop.css: the .develop-still fallback inset is corrected to 4.4% 5.5%. Also added the lifted-print state and the styles for the negative image.
experiment.json: description, tags (WebGL, Shaders, Simulation) and intent updated; status is still candidate and building is false.
polish.remaining: All three checks pass: lab-gate prints PASS, the compile check prints PASS (9 modules), and every shader in the GLSL check is ok. Nothing was run in a browser, as the rules required. The look of the first frame comes from my CPU prototype, which uses the engine's constants (G 6000, 480 substeps, friction 1.2, cockle 0.08), not from a GPU render. The new GPU paths are untested: the fence-based stats readback, the half-float pending-time channel and the reduced-motion still mask. They were checked by reading the code only. Thumbnails are 112x140 (the plate's 4:5) and shown with cover in the existing 56x72 cell to keep the 4px grid, so there is a tiny crop. Relevant files: /Users/herb/Documents/GitHub/portfolio/src/app/lab/develop/DevelopStage.jsx, developEngine.js, developShader.js, DevelopExperience.jsx, DevelopBench.jsx, developSources.js, develop.css, experiment.json.

recheck.firstFrame: I checked this with a CPU port of the exact flux, height and develop passes (144-wide grid, the same INTRO_STEPS and 0.95s pre-sim). The paper-white 4:5 plate fades in over 900ms already mid-wave. A warm amber film (blue cut by up to about 9%) covers the lower-left ~55% of the sheet. Its soft diagonal front runs from the upper-left edge down to the lower-right, with a thin 8% darker rim and the water's broken reflections. Under the water, John's beard, glasses, the left hair and the black background corners are 50-75% developed, while the skin is still almost paper-white (about 10% of its density). The upper-right (right hair, forehead) is blank paper. So the reveal really is the brief's shadows-first diagonal, and the previous round's 'face already fully developed' problem is gone. The scripted slosh keeps running live for 1.25s after reveal, and the lower-left deepens on its own to nearly finished (blacks ~94%, midtones ~60%) as the water drains to a permanent pool along the bottom edge. The timer rolls 0:00 -> 0:02. The weak point you see at once is softness: john.webp is 200x200, so a 156x200 crop is shown about 7x enlarged and then passed through a cubic B-spline filter, which smooths it further.
recheck.checks: lab-gate develop: PASS. lab-compile-check develop: PASS (9 modules). lab-glsl-check: all 10 shader strings ok (FULLSCREEN_VERTEX, COCKLE, RESET, STILL, FLUX, HEIGHT, DEVELOP, FIELD, STATS, PRINT). Previous round: all four findings verified fixed. (1) Development is now steeply shadows-first, using pow(exposure, 1.8), and the reveal shows a true diagonal. The pre-sim is still 0.95s with a 0.12 lean rather than the suggested 0.6s and 0.08, but the result is correct. (2) retireTo now awaits loadSource and passes the loaded image into api.retire -> freshSheet -> setImage before resetSheet, and the next two sources are warmed 900ms after ready. (3) IDLE_STOP_MS is 8000, and the idle develop runs at 12fps on setTimeout(83). (4) Stats use a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER plus fenceSync, polled with clientWaitSync(0) and read with getBufferSubData. CPU-port stability check: a max hold, release and a 3 uv/s flick gave no NaN, max depth 1.3, h >= 0, and no checkerboarding.

issues.problem: Holding still does not bring the developer to your finger. leanToward makes the tilt proportional to the finger's distance from the plate centre, so a press on John's eyes (around 0.5, 0.6) gives only a ~0.04 rad tilt. The water creeps up for over a second, passes under the finger and pools at the far edge. The paddle (FLUX_FRAGMENT uPaddle) only takes max() of existing flux, scaled by depth, so it does nothing on dry paper. The hint says 'Hold the sheet where the developer should run', but the developer never gathers where you hold. The cause is still a remote tray tilt, which was the herb skeptic's main complaint.
issues.fix: Add a press well: the finger pushes the paper down into the bath. In FLUX_FRAGMENT's bedAt (and in HEIGHT if the bed is referenced there), subtract uPress * exp(-dot(o,o)/(r*r)), where o = (uv - uPaddle.xy) * vec2(0.8, 1.0), r = 0.11 and uPress eases 0 -> 1.6 over about 120ms while pointer.active (set it in setPaddle). Drop POINTER_REACH to about 0.5 so the tilt only helps the water head that way. The bath then runs into the dip and follows the finger as a blob, so dragging leaves a developed trail. Release lets the well spring back and the water slosh out, so the flick keeps working.

issues.problem: The default print is mushy. /cast/john.webp is 200x200 and cropFor keeps 156x200 of it. On a 1440x900 screen the plate is 566x708 CSS px at DPR 2, about 7x enlargement. sampleSpline is a cubic B-spline, which is an approximating filter, so it blurs the source by roughly another half texel on top of that. Every silver edge (the glasses rims, the eyes) reaches the visitor as a smear. Grain hides some of it but not the eyes.
issues.fix: Sample uImage with a sharpening reconstruction rather than a B-spline. Use the 9-tap Catmull-Rom (or 5-tap bicubic-sharp) variant, or compute tone from bilinear plus an unsharp term: tone += (tone - toneFromMipLevel1) * 0.7. Better still, ship a 640px john source (e.g. /cast/john-640.webp) and keep the 200px file for the negative chip.

issues.problem: The intro's third step (-0.03, -0.03) keeps the water spread over the lower-left until t = 2.2s, and soak adds about 0.9s on top. By the time a visitor reaches for the plate, about 60% of the sheet has mean T >= 2, so the skin and midtones there are already in. The brief's 'rock back and the midtones fill in like breath' then only happens in the upper-right third.
issues.fix: End the scripted slosh sooner: change the third INTRO_STEPS entry to { until: 1.25, x: -0.02, y: REST_LEAN_Y } so the water starts draining right after reveal. Optionally lower the 0.7s lean to y 0.10, keeping the reveal diagonal but holding the left half at shadows only.

issues.problem: Eight seconds after the last input, development and fog freeze, so leaving it 'too long' never fogs. The timer stops, yet the status still reads 'Developing' and the bottom pool still shows as wet. That breaks the brief's 'leave it too long and the whites slowly fog, and you realise you are actually making a print'.
issues.fix: On the full page only (!embedded), keep a cheap develop and render on setTimeout(500) while peakSeconds < 30, then stop. Embedded keeps the hard stop. Alternatively, when the loop parks, swap the status MorphText to 'Resting' so the label never lies.

issues.problem: `moving` includes gyro.on. With 'Use tilt' enabled, a phone runs the full 60fps loop (8 sim substeps x 2 passes plus a full-resolution print) for as long as the page is open, even lying still on a table.
issues.fix: Remove gyro.on from `moving`. In handleOrientation, call wake() only when |gyro.x - lastGyroX| + |gyro.y - lastGyroY| > 0.003 rad. Energy and offTarget then park the loop once the phone is still.

issues.problem: capture() restores the screen with render(1) unconditionally. With reduced motion (water() = 0) the loop is usually parked, so pressing Save PNG or Next sheet leaves the wet sheen and amber tint on screen, which that mode otherwise never shows.
issues.fix: Give capture a restore argument, capture(context, w, h, water), and end it with render(water). DevelopStage passes water().

issues.problem: Nine programs are compiled and linked with an immediate COMPILE_STATUS / LINK_STATUS query after each one. That forces synchronous compilation on the main thread at mount, a visible hitch on phones and in the experiments index where several pieces mount together.
issues.fix: Enable KHR_parallel_shader_compile. Issue every compile and link first, then check COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR on later frames (or check status once after all links), and run reveal() only when all programs are complete.

issues.problem: .develop-negative hard-codes background-color #d8d6d1, and .develop-row__unit (line 207) uses margin-left: 1px, which is off the 4px grid.
issues.fix: Use var(--color-surface-sunken) for the negative placeholder. Drop the 1px margin, since the unit glyph sits fine flush, or use a thin space in the markup.

issues.problem: Below 900px, Controls opens a fixed bottom sheet with no Escape handling, no focus move into it and no focus return. A keyboard or switch user tabs through the hidden page behind it.
issues.fix: When it opens, focus the first preset chip. Add a keydown listener that closes the sheet on Escape and returns focus to the Controls button, and mark .develop-stage inert while the sheet is open.

issues.problem: Stored params pass sanitise by type only and are never clamped. A depth of 0.3 saved from the brief-era 0.15-0.5 slider (or a hand-edited value) loads as a pool four times deeper, which floods half the sheet at rest and puts the slider thumb off the track.
issues.fix: In readStoredParams, clamp each DEVELOP_CONTROLS key to its [min, max] after loadStored.

recheck.wowGap: Make the finger press the paper into the bath. While held, a soft well about 0.11 wide and 1.6 deep under the pointer is subtracted from the bed in FLUX_FRAGMENT's bedAt, and POINTER_REACH drops to about 0.5. The amber developer then visibly runs to your fingertip, pools there, and follows as you drag, so John's eyes come up in warm black exactly where you pressed and nowhere else. Release springs the well out and the pool sloshes back across the face. That turns the 'remote tray tilt' into cause under the finger, the one upgrade both skeptics asked for.

changes: Press well (wowGap): FLUX_FRAGMENT bedAt now subtracts uPress.z * exp(-|(uv - press) * (0.8, 1)|^2 / 0.11^2), so the finger pushes the paper into the bath. The engine eases the press 0 -> 1.6 (tau 40ms, about 120ms) while held and springs it back on release, so the water sloshes back out
POINTER_REACH dropped 1.15 -> 0.5, so the tilt only helps the water head toward the finger and the well captures it, follows a drag and leaves a developed trail
A tap keeps the well under the tap point for 800ms (pointer.holdUntil), and the loop stays live while the press is easing
PRINT shader shades a soft paper dimple under the finger (light from upper left, about 5%), giving a cue on dry paper. It is scaled by water, so saved PNGs and reduced motion do not show it
Reduced motion: the STILL pass wets a disc under the press, so holding develops right under the finger with no visible wave
Image sharpness: replaced the B-spline image read with a 9-tap Catmull-Rom (textureGrad, so the mip choice is correct), plus a 0.5 acutance unsharp term against a mip read one level softer
Intro: the scripted slosh now ends at 1.25s. Steps up to 0.95s are unchanged, so the judged first frame stays the same, and from reveal the water drains toward rest at (-0.02, REST_LEAN_Y)
