Idle fog: the full page keeps developing on a 500ms timer after 8s idle, while peak mean T < 30s and idle < 120s, so the pool still fogs and the timer rolls. When the loop finally parks (and always when embedded) the status changes to 'Resting', and it returns to Developing on any wake
Gyro: removed gyro.on from `moving`. handleOrientation calls wake() only when the change exceeds 0.003 rad, so a still phone parks the loop
capture(context, w, h, water) restores with render(water). Save PNG and Next sheet pass water(), so reduced motion no longer flashes the wet sheen

Shader compile: programs are compiled and linked without status queries and KHR_parallel_shader_compile is enabled. engine.prepare() is polled on rAF (COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR, otherwise one status check after all links). resetSheet and reveal wait for it, and setSettings skips runHeight until it is linked
CSS: .develop-negative uses var(--color-surface-sunken), and the 1px .develop-row__unit margin is gone

Mobile Controls sheet: role=dialog and aria-modal when open. Focus moves to the first preset chip, Escape or Done closes it and returns focus to the Controls button (after commit), and .develop-stage is inert while open (only below 900px)
readStoredParams clamps every DEVELOP_CONTROLS key to its [min, max] and falls back to the default if a value is non-finite
Hint, aria label, page metadata and experiment.json description/intent now describe the press: 'Press the sheet and the developer runs to your finger.' building is false, status is candidate
polish2.remaining: Not checked in a browser, per the rules. I traced it by hand only. The press depth (1.6) and radius (0.11) follow the review. At the default 0.08 depth the well holds almost the whole bath, so the rest of the sheet drains while you hold. That is the intended blob-follows-finger behaviour, but PRESS_DEPTH in developEngine.js is the knob if it feels too greedy. No higher-resolution John source was added, because writes are limited to the lab folder. Sharpness comes from Catmull-Rom plus acutance instead.

build.summary: Quadtree turns Herb's recently played covers (imageLarge at 640px, centre-cropped to 512²) into a quadtree mosaic of rounded tiles. Each node's colour and error come in O(1) from six Float64 summed-area tables, which are built across two idle slices, and the resting tree is the 560 highest-priority Fogleman splits. Under the pointer the lens splits tiles towards real pixels: how deep it goes depends on how long you dwell and how fast you move, so a slow pass sharpens almost to the pixel and a fast whip stays chunky. Detail folds back up deepest-first 1.4s after you leave, while press-and-drag (hold, on touch) carves detail in permanently, with a rolling 'carved' count and a Release pill. Clicking morphs one cover's tree into the next from the click point (shared nodes recolour with a pulse, missing ones split in, extra ones merge out), and all tiles render in two instanced WebGL2 draws. Those draws read a free-list slot buffer through one bufferSubData per frame and animate in the vertex shader from a 64-entry spring table, so animating tiles cost the CPU nothing.
build.wowMoment: After the opening cascade, the piece shows off on its own with a lens sweep through the cover's most detailed area: a slow sweep that sharpens a face or lettering down towards the pixels while flat sky stays as fat soft tiles, and then that detail folds back up behind it. Then you click a cover and the mosaic reorganises its own structure into the next album, starting from where you clicked.
build.knownIssues: The piece has never run in a browser, as instructed. What was checked: all three checks pass, glslc compiles both shaders (as GLSL 310 es), and a headless Node simulation of QuadField ran the intro, a sweep, a dwell, merge-back, carving, a morph and a release with no slot leaks or holes in the tree. The loop also went fully idle afterwards: intro took about 1.7s including a 0.36s hold, a morph about 1.8s, and the worst frame was about 8ms on a deliberately noisy synthetic image. The WebGL2 draw calls, the CSS lens ring (mix-blend difference, cqw sizing) and the final layout at 1280px and on phones still need checking by eye. The Canvas2D fallback draws flat tiles with no animation. In development StrictMode each cover's tables are built twice because the cover cache is cleared and rebuilt on remount; production is unaffected. Mouse carving starts after 240ms or 6px of movement, so a quick click always means "next cover". page.js was changed to prefer imageLarge, and its metadata description was shortened. Count totals depend on each cover's detail: the resting tree stops splitting flat regions whose error is below 2.5.

critique.firstFrame: The page loads with a sunken square of the right size. Once the cover decodes, it is replaced by one rounded tile in the cover's average colour. That tile pops in on the spring, coloured from the page surface towards the mean, and the canvas fades in over 900ms. At about 0.36s it splits into four quadrant tiles. Those four then sit still for about 0.44s, because the intro wave tests each node's centre, and the quadrant centres are 0.35 cover-widths from the origin. After that the cascade runs outward. It settles at around 1.5s into a mosaic of about 1,680 rounded tiles with proportional gaps: fat soft tiles in flat areas and small ones on faces and lettering. About 0.5s later the demo lens sweeps across the busiest row, sharpens it, and the detail folds back 1.4s afterwards. The settled mosaic is a strong frame for the vote. The pause between one tile and four is the only weak beat.
critique.checks:
All three checks pass. lab-gate printed "PASS quadtree". compile-check printed "PASS compile quadtree (10 modules)". glsl-check reported ok for both shaders in quadtreeShader.js (lines 3 and 113). Both shaders are plain strings with no interpolation, so the GLSL check covers them fully.

I also read through the GPU and asset code and found no blockers:
- The vertex attribute layout (locations 0 to 4, stride 48, divisors) matches the 12-float slot.
- uSpring[64] is found through getActiveUniform and set with uniform1fv. The spring is clamped past its end, and negative ages are hidden.
- Freed slots get size 0 and are culled to a degenerate clip position. The draw count is highWater.
- Retiring parents wait for deferred frees, so a merge has the children and the parent alive at the same time.
- Context restore re-uploads the whole CPU buffer.
- destroy() deletes the VAO, buffers and program, then calls loseContext.
- The observers and listeners are cleaned up, React StrictMode double-mounting is safe because each mount makes a fresh canvas, and nothing touches window during the server render.
- The /cast and /flyout assets exist, imageLarge is used, and non-square images are centre-cropped before the summed-area tables are built.

issues.problem: .qt-lens has will-change: transform, which makes it its own stacking context, and stacking contexts are isolated groups. The ring and the dot use mix-blend-mode: difference, but they can only blend with the empty .qt-lens layer, never with the canvas. They draw as plain white at 0.86 opacity. On light or white parts of a cover the ring disappears, and with cursor: none on fine pointers the visitor loses their cursor entirely over those areas.
issues.fix: Remove will-change from .qt-lens and write the translate3d straight onto .qt-lens__ring and a real dot element, so the blend reaches the canvas. Or drop the blend and draw the ring as two layers: a 1.5px ink ring inside a 1px white halo. Either way it stays readable on any tile colour.

issues.problem: applyResolution sets canvas.width and height, which clears the drawing buffer. The context has alpha: false, so a cleared buffer shows as opaque black. This happens in two places. The ResizeObserver callback runs after rAF and before paint. The governor resize at line 957 runs right after draw() in the same frame. Both present a black square for one frame. That flash happens on every window-resize tick, every panel toggle between 900 and 1099px, and every time the governor changes resolution during a heavy cascade on a slow phone.
issues.fix: In applyResolution, when the size changes, call this.draw(this.now()) synchronously right after setting the size (if there is a program or 2D context and coverPx is above 0). In frame(), call governor.sample and applyResolution before draw(), not after.

issues.problem: Wheel sizing breaks on trackpads. handleWheel stores the unrounded lens value in lensControlRef and commits a value rounded to 0.01. The commit creates a new params object, which creates a new handleLens, which re-runs the sync effect, which resets lensControlRef.value to the rounded params.lens. On a MacBook trackpad each wheel event moves the lens by less than 0.005, so every tick rounds back to the same value and the lens never changes. Each tick also writes to localStorage and re-renders the whole panel.
issues.fix: Keep the live value in its own ref, for example liveLensRef. Only resync it from params.lens when Math.abs(params.lens - liveLensRef.current) > 0.006, which means the slider or a reset changed it. Commit unrounded, or round only for display. Write to localStorage through a 200ms trailing debounce in commit.

issues.problem: waveReached and waveDelay measure distance to the node's centre. In the intro, the root splits at 0.36s, but the four quadrant centres are 0.354 away from the origin, so they wait until about 0.80s. The first impression is a stall: four big flat tiles hold for close to half a second. The cover-change morph has the same effect: large nodes far from the click lag.
issues.fix: Measure the distance to the nearest point of the node's rectangle: dx = max(left - wx, 0, wx - left - size), and the same for dy. Nodes that contain the origin then react immediately and the cascade flows outward without a pause. Keep the centre distance for the recolour stagger if that order looks better.

issues.problem: When the governor changes resolution inside frame(), applyResolution calls wake(). By then this.raf is 0, so a rAF gets scheduled. The end of frame() then schedules a second one and overwrites the handle. Two frame() calls run in the next frame, and the orphaned handle cannot be cancelled by setActive(false).
issues.fix: Guard the scheduling at the end of frame() with `if (!this.raf)`, or skip wake() in applyResolution when it is called from inside a frame.

issues.problem: If getContext('webgl2') succeeds but createResources throws (a driver compile or link failure), the code sets gl to null and asks the same canvas for getContext('2d'). That returns null because the canvas already has a WebGL context. The Canvas2D fallback silently draws nothing, so the cover stays blank.
issues.fix: When createResources throws, call loseContext, replace the canvas with a fresh element (or have the constructor accept a factory), and request the 2D context from the new one.

issues.problem: panelOpen comes from a useSyncExternalStore media query whose server snapshot is false. At 1100px and wider, the server HTML renders with the panel closed and a wide cover placeholder. After hydration the grid column snaps to 296px and the placeholder visibly shrinks.
issues.fix: Make the default panel state pure CSS: a @media (min-width: 1100px) rule opens the panel unless data-panel="closed" is set. Only set data-panel after the visitor toggles it.

issues.problem: Switching between the Tiles, Discs and Pixels presets changes uShape, gap and radius in a single frame. It is an instant state swap in a piece whose whole point is transitions.
issues.fix: Tween the gap, radius and shape uniforms on the CPU over 280ms with the house ease, using a shapeMix float in the shader to blend corner radius towards halfPx. Or ride the change on a recolour-style wave from the centre so tiles re-form outward.

issues.problem: If Spotify fails, the fallback covers are titled 'Card 01' to 'Card 12' by 'Local scans', which reads as placeholder text under the hero.
issues.fix: Give the fallback covers real titles and credits, from public/flyout/CREDITS.md, or reuse the names the flyout page uses.

issues.problem: While the summed-area tables build, the readout shows '0 tiles'. It is an empty number in the loading state, and it then rolls up from zero.
issues.fix: Hide the tile item, or show it at the well's opacity state, until the first onStats call that has a non-zero count. Let it roll up from 1 together with the intro.

issues.problem: Each cached source holds six Float64 tables of 513² entries, about 12.6MB. KEEP = 3, plus the field's current source and a prefetch, comes to about 50MB on a phone.
issues.fix: Use KEEP = 2. Store red, green and blue sums as Float32 (they are exact up to 2^24 × 255) and keep only the squared sums in Float64. That roughly halves the memory.

critique.wowGap: Make the lens push into the mosaic even where nothing splits. At the moment, flat sky under the pointer does nothing, and with the ring blend bug the visitor sees no response at all over plain areas. Add uPointer (in cover units) and uLensRadius uniforms to the vertex shader. Compute w = 1 - smoothstep(0, uLensRadius, distance from the tile centre to the pointer). For tiles 4px and larger, open each tile's gap by an extra 0.06 × size × w, round its corners further towards halfPx × 0.35 × w, and nudge it outward from the pointer by 0.02 × size × w. Ease uPointer on the CPU with a 60ms critically damped follow, so the mosaic visibly parts and breathes around the cursor like a flat loupe. It costs nothing on the CPU and stays flat Swiss, with no 3D. The error-driven splits then land inside a region that already feels alive, so the first hover reads as touching a material rather than tripping a filter.

changes: wowGap, quadtreeShader.js and QuadField.js: added uPointer, uLensRadius and uLensAmount to the vertex shader. Tiles 4px and up near the lens get w = 1 - smoothstep(0, R, d). Their gap opens by 0.06 x size x w, corners round 0.35 x w of the way towards halfPx, and the tile moves 0.02 x size x w away from the pointer. So the mosaic parts around the cursor even over flat areas where nothing splits.

QuadField.followLens: the pointer feeding the shader follows on a 60ms critically damped spring. The push fades in over 140ms and out over 320ms, and the radius eases when you press. It snaps on entry and under reduced motion. Frames keep running only while it settles, and the demo sweep shows the parting too.

quadtree.css: removed mix-blend-mode from the lens. The ring is now a 1.5px ink ring between two 1px white halos (outer and inset box-shadow), and the dot is ink with a white halo. Both read on any tile colour. Ring opacity raised to 1 (0.64 during the demo).
QuadField.applyResolution(paintNow): after resizing the canvas it draws synchronously in the same callback (ResizeObserver or panel toggle), so no black frame appears. It no longer calls wake().

QuadField.frame: governor.sample and applyResolution now run before draw(). The rAF at the end of the frame is only scheduled when this.raf is 0 (and the field is active and not lost), so frames are no longer doubled and no handle is orphaned.

QuadStage wheel: the live value is kept in liveLensRef and committed unrounded through onLensRef. It is resynced from params.lens only when the difference is over 0.006 and no wheel sizing is in progress. Clamped no-op ticks return early. Arrow keys step from the live value.
QuadtreeExperience.commit: localStorage writes go through a 200ms trailing debounce. Reset cancels any pending write, and both timers are cleared on unmount.

QuadField waves: waveDistance now measures to the nearest point of the node's rect. waveReached, merge order and split priority use it, so nodes containing the origin react at once and the four-quadrant stall in the intro is gone. The recolour stagger still uses centreDelay.

QuadField.openWebGL: if createResources throws, it deletes resources, calls loseContext, swaps in a fresh canvas element (replaceCanvas) and asks that one for the 2D context. Listeners are attached to the live canvas, and QuadStage cleanup removes field.canvas.

Panel default is now pure CSS. Below 1100px it is closed; at 1100px and up a media query opens it unless data-panel="closed". data-panel is set only after the visitor toggles. The toggle label switches via CSS spans, so nothing snaps after hydration.

Preset look tween: gap, radius, disc and outline are blended on the CPU over 280ms with cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). uShape is replaced by uDisc and uOutline mix uniforms. The tween runs only when the shape changes or both gap and radius change, so a slider being dragged is never tweened. The Canvas2D fallback reads the same look values.
page.js: the 12 fallback covers now carry real player names and series credits from public/flyout/CREDITS.md.
QuadReadout: the tile count is hidden until the first non-zero onStats. Then it scales and blurs in and SlotNumber mounts at the first value instead of rolling up from 0.

quadTree.js and coverLibrary.js: the red, green and blue sums are now Uint32Array, which stays exact (the max is 66.8M). The three squared tables are merged into one Float64 squares table, since only the summed variance is used. That cuts each source from about 12.6MB to 5.3MB, and KEEP is now 2.
experiment.json: description, tags (WebGL, Shaders, Music) and intent updated. building is false, status is still candidate.
polish.remaining: I fixed every issue the reviewer listed. Nothing was checked in a browser, as the rules required; all I verified is that the three checks pass and the code reads correctly. Two calls of mine are worth checking on the page. First, I kept the lens push under reduced motion: it snaps to the pointer instead of easing, rather than being switched off. Second, I used Uint32 for the colour sums instead of the reviewer's Float32, because Float32 loses precision above 16.7M, which would have broken variance in small regions near the bottom-right of the cover.

recheck.firstFrame: Server render shows the title, the hint and a sunken placeholder well at cover size, inset 4% with a 12px radius. The cover's title and artist are already in the meta row. useNearViewport resolves after one IntersectionObserver report, so QuadStage mounts. The cover image is fetched and decoded, and the summed-area tables are built across two idle slices. A single rounded root tile in the cover's mean colour then pops in. It is inset by gap/2 = 4%, which lines up with the well. About 0.36s later it cascades out from the centre in pinwheel pops over roughly 1.2s, and the tile count rolls up. About 0.5s after the cascade settles, a ghost ring sweeps across the busiest row of the image. It parts the mosaic and leaves a wake of sharp detail, which folds back 1.4s later. That self-demo is a genuinely strong first five seconds. Two things are weak. The root pop is mostly swallowed because it plays while the canvas is still fading in over 900ms. The root also starts from the surface colour, which is lighter than the sunken well it replaces, so there is a faint light-then-dark flicker at the handoff. The settled frame is a crisp chunky mosaic of the real cover on a matching #f1f5f9 ground with no visible canvas box.
recheck.checks: All three pass. lab-gate quadtree: PASS (lint, comments, type, tokens). lab-compile-check quadtree: PASS (10 modules bundled). lab-glsl-check src/app/lab/quadtree: ok for both shaders (quadtreeShader.js:3 vertex, :124 fragment). Previous-round fixes were verified in the code. (1) The ring no longer uses mix-blend. It is a 1.5px ink border with outer and inset 1px white halos, and the dot is ink with a white halo, so it reads on any tile colour. (2) applyResolution(paintNow) redraws synchronously after resizing the backing store from the ResizeObserver path. In frame(), the governor resize now runs before draw(), so the black-frame flash is gone. (3) Wheel sizing keeps liveLensRef, resyncs only when the difference exceeds 0.006 and not while sizing, commits unrounded, and debounces localStorage by 200ms, so it works on trackpads. The previous wowGap is implemented: the vertex shader gets uPointer, uLensRadius and uLensAmount; tiles 4px and up get +0.06×size gap, corners eased 35% toward round, and a 0.02×size outward push; the CPU follow is critically damped with a 60ms constant and fades in and out.

issues.problem: Colour snaps on the cover-change wave front. recolour() writes the new mean into aColour and keeps the old colour in aFrom until the wave reaches the tile's centre (centreDelay). split() and merge() fire earlier, when the wave reaches the rect edge (waveDelay). On split, the retiring parent (kind 1) renders aColour, which is the new colour, at once. Its children pop from that new colour too. On merge, each child (kind 2) blends from its new colour, which was never shown. So every big tile that changes structure cuts hard from the old cover to the new one, while untouched tiles ease over 200ms. For a 0.5-cover tile the gap is up to about 0.22s. Rapid clicks mid-morph also start from targets rather than from what is on screen.
issues.fix: Add displayedColour(slot, time, out). For kind 4 it returns aFrom when time < t0, and otherwise mix(aFrom, aColour, smoothstep of (time − t0)/0.2). For any other kind it returns aColour. In split(), write the displayed colour into the parent's 3..5 before retiring it, and use it as the children's aFrom. In merge(), write each child's displayed colour into 3..5 before setting kind 2. In recolour(), use the displayed colour as aFrom instead of data[at+3..5].

issues.problem: The 900ms canvas opacity reveal overlaps the root tile's pop at t0 = now + 40ms, so the opening spring is seen at 10–40% opacity. The root also blends from SURFACE (#f1f5f9) while the well it replaces is surface-sunken (#e9edf3), so the handoff flickers light then dark.
issues.fix: Shorten the canvas fade to 240ms or drop it, because the well already masks the load. Start the root about 120ms later (startAt = time + 0.12). Blend the root from the sunken colour: in QuadField, set SURFACE_SUNKEN = [233/255, 237/255, 243/255] and pass it as fromRed/Green/Blue in setCover's first branch.

issues.problem: Each wheel event calls onLens, then commit, then setEdited. That re-renders the whole experience at trackpad rate (60–120Hz), including the panel's eight SlotNumber sliders. It also creates a new params object, which runs setParams, retargetLook and refreshLevels, and it animates the ring through a CSS width/height transition, which triggers layout.
issues.fix: While sizing, push the live value straight to the field (fieldRef.current.setLens(next)) and set --qt-lens on the cover element imperatively. Commit to React state once, in the sizingTimer trailing callback. Animate the ring size with transform: scale instead of width/height.

issues.problem: busy includes this.inside, so rAF runs every frame for as long as the pointer rests on the cover. Every 250ms, LENS_REFRESH re-walks the lens. The brief asks for zero cost at idle, and a resting pointer is the common reading posture.
issues.fix: Drop this.inside from busy. Keep the loop alive only while moved, lensBusy, focus not settled (|target − focus| > 0.01), lensSettling, or animating. setPointer and setPressed already call wake().

issues.problem: The dirty range is coalesced as min..max. With a LIFO free list, reused slots are scattered across the buffer, so a heavy carve or a morph can upload most of the high-water range every frame. At 30k tiles that is about 1.4MB per frame, which is heavy on phones. highWater also never shrinks, so after a release both passes keep drawing tens of thousands of zeroed instances.
issues.fix: Fill freed slots lowest-first: keep the free stack sorted, or use a min-heap or bitset scan. Live tiles then stay packed near zero. When the top slots are free, lower highWater (while highWater > 0 and slot highWater−1 is free, decrement). Optionally track two dirty spans and upload them separately when the gap between them is large.

issues.problem: compact and dprCap are decided once, at mount, from cover.clientWidth. If a phone rotates to landscape, a window resizes across 520px, or the panel toggles, the field keeps the wrong lens scale, minimum tile (×1.5) and DPR cap.
issues.fix: Recompute compact in the ResizeObserver callback. Add field.setCompact(compact, dprCap) to update this.compact and this.dprCap, and to toggle data-compact on the cover. Call refreshLevels() after it.

issues.problem: The cover is a focusable element with role="img" that handles Space, Enter, the arrow keys and Escape. Screen readers treat img as non-interactive, so the keyboard affordances are announced only through a long aria-label. ArrowUp/Down resize the lens with no visual feedback, because data-sizing is not set.
issues.fix: Use role="application" with aria-roledescription="quadtree cover", and keep the title and artist as the label. Put the key help in aria-describedby pointing at the visible hint. In the ArrowUp/Down branch, set data-sizing and clear it on the same 700ms timer the wheel uses, and place the ring at the cover centre if no pointer is inside.

issues.problem: .qt-release uses padding: 0 10px, which is off the 4px grid. The well and canvas radii are hard-coded at 12px rather than taken from a radius token.
issues.fix: Use padding: 0 12px (or 8px). Use var(--radius-md) or the matching token for .qt-cover__well instead of 12px.

recheck.wowGap: Make the cover change one unbroken re-organisation, because it is the moment repeated on every click and the one nobody has seen before. First, carry each tile's on-screen colour into split, merge and recolour (see the first issue), so the front never cuts. Second, drive everything from a single delay per node, waveDelay (rect-edge distance from the click / 1.6). The recolour start, the split time and the merge time should all use it, so colour easing, child pops and fold-ups land as one soft front sweeping out from the click. Third, give the front a lead: for 120ms before a node's delay, ease its gap open by +0.05×size and its corner towards 0.35×half. Use the existing press path in the vertex shader, driven by a per-instance 'front' timestamp in aTiming.z, which is currently the unused level slot. The old mosaic then visibly loosens, re-tints and re-knits into the new album's structure in one pass. That is the engineer's tree-to-tree morph finished to the edge, and it is still not a ring ripple.

build.summary: Mosh simulates a P-frame datamosh on Herb's recent covers, in raw WebGL2. A small CPU motion-vector field, one cell per macroblock, takes in your pointer strokes through a Gaussian brush. Each frame it decays the vectors (τ 1.4s), bleeds 4% into neighbouring cells, and turns the motion into whole-pixel shifts, carrying the fractional remainder forward. The GPU pass then copies whole pixels with texelFetch: luma moves by each block's vector, chroma by the averaged 4:2:0 vector, and anything that slides in from off the edge is taken from the next cover. A residual pulls each moving block towards the next cover's average colour for that block, read from a mip level, and fast blocks also get quantised 4×4 detail, so the colour arrives in hard squares. A keyframe (tap, Space, the button or a cover chip) sweeps diagonally across the frame, and each block resolves through the target cover's mips, 16→8→4px→sharp, before the stream moves to the next record. Next to the plate are the title, morphing Now playing / Next captions, a rolling frame counter, six cover chips with a sliding underline, and a codec panel. The panel has H.264, MPEG-2, Bloom and Slab presets plus a Tune drawer: block size, persistence, residual, ringing, a 4:2:0 chroma switch and a show-vectors switch.
build.wowMoment: The page opens on a half-moshed cover: a diagonal smear of stair-stepped slabs, already in the next record's colours, that depixelates in from the top-left and keeps sliding. Hovering shows a lens of codec macroblock dots around the cursor. Dragging brings up the whole motion-vector field as round-capped ink ticks pushing the slabs as you paint them. One tap snaps the frame clean in a diagonal sweep of blocks going 16px to 8px to 4px to sharp, landing on the next album.
build.knownIssues: It has never been run in a browser (not allowed here). All four checks pass: the lab gate, the compile check, the GLSL parse check and ESLint. But no GLSL ES 3.00 compiler exists on this machine, so a shader compile error would only show at runtime. If one happens, the page shows the WebGL2 failure state and the static cover. Motion constants were tuned by reasoning, not by looking, and may need a pass in the browser: drag gain 0.55, a 14px/frame cap scaled to the buffer, intro swipe gain 0.24 and residual 0.035/frame. At default persistence a fast swipe will smear the cover into streaks within a few seconds. Deviations from the brief: raw WebGL2 instead of R3F; a 640² buffer on desktop and 512² on phones (brief said 512 and 384), so Spotify's 640px covers map 1:1; the stream is the first 6 covers so the six chips cover the whole loop; and the plate reveals with a shader depixelate instead of a fade. page.js now passes imageLarge. Clamp-to-edge smearing was replaced: pixels shifted in from off the plate are filled from the next cover in place. Space and the arrow keys work when the plate is focused or nothing else on the page has focus.

critique.firstFrame: In production the first frame works and looks good. The server renders the quiet Swiss layout: a plate on the sunken token with a softly pulsing dot grid, and a side column that rises in with a blur stagger. Once the first two covers decode, 40 pre-simulated frames of the scripted diagonal swipe are baked in. The plate then resolves out of paper in a 900ms top-left diagonal sweep of 32px cells, stepping down the mip levels 5, 4, 3, 2 to sharp, while the half-moshed stair-stepped band keeps sliding and the counter rolls up from about 040. In dev, where Herb votes at localhost /taste, he will almost certainly see something else. Next's app router turns React StrictMode on by default (define-env.js), so MoshStage's effect runs, cleans up and runs again on the same JSX <canvas>. The cleanup calls WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext(), so the second getContext('webgl2') gets the same context back, already lost. shaderSource(null) or getShaderParameter then throws, onError fires, and the plate shows the static CSS cover with 'This plate needs WebGL2'. As shipped, the vote frame is an error state.
critique.checks: 1. node scripts/lab-gate.mjs mosh printed PASS. 2. compile-check.mjs mosh printed PASS (7 modules). 3. glsl-check.mjs src/app/lab/mosh printed ok for all 4 shaders (TRIANGLE_VERTEX, ENCODE, ADVECT, DISPLAY), with no interpolated chunks. I also checked by hand that every uniform each program declares is set every pass, that ivec shifts and texelFetch levels stay in range for 640² and 512² buffers (non-power-of-two mips divide exactly to level 7), and that the vUv varying matches. The RGBA16F render target is gated on EXT_color_buffer_float with an RGBA8 fallback, and the RGBA32F field texture is only read with NEAREST and texelFetch. None of the pairs in the advect and display passes forms a feedback loop.

issues.problem: The <canvas> is JSX, so it lives through React's effect re-runs, but dispose() calls loseContext() on it (moshEngine.js:1078). StrictMode is on by default in the app router in dev, so the mount, cleanup, mount cycle hands the second createMoshEngine a lost context. createShader returns null and buildGpu throws, so the plate falls back to a static cover with 'This plate needs WebGL2'. The same thing happens in prod whenever the effect re-runs, for example when the OS reduced-motion setting is toggled.
issues.fix: Do what the sibling pieces (marble, develop, taffy) do. Remove the JSX canvas, create it inside the effect (document.createElement('canvas'), className 'mosh-canvas', aria-hidden, prepend it to surfaceRef) and remove it in cleanup after engine.dispose(). Each run then gets a fresh context, and loseContext stays safe.

issues.problem: resize() sets canvas.width inside the ResizeObserver callback and only renders on the next rAF. Resizing a WebGL canvas clears its drawing buffer, and with alpha:false that is opaque black. ResizeObserver runs after rAF in the same frame, so the cleared buffer gets composited. Every window-resize step and every governor-free size change flashes the plate black for a frame.
issues.fix: In resize(), after applyResolution(), draw straight away when ready: `if (seeded && gpu && active) render(performance.now());`. Inside render, skip the reveal-time bookkeeping when reveal is already 1, so the draw is just a repaint.

issues.problem: The 'codec ringing' is not quantised. acStep is rounded to 20/255, then multiplied by ringGate, which is about 0.13 per frame at the default 0.6. The visible step is about 0.01, applied every frame, so any block moving faster than 3px per frame eases smoothly toward the target's 4px mosaic (98% after 30 frames). A fast swipe therefore reads as a pixelated crossfade into cover B and wipes out A's structure. The brief and both skeptics named this as the main risk: structure must stay legible.
issues.fix: Make the gate a per-block event, not a blend. Pass a uFrame int and apply the full quantised acStep only when hash(block + uFrame) < ringGate, for example `if (fract(sin(dot(vec2(block)+float(uFrame)*0.618, vec2(12.9898,78.233)))*43758.5453) < ringGate) ycc += acStep * vec3(1.0,0.5,0.5);`. Ringing then arrives as hard 20/255 steps in scattered blocks. Lower the default ringing to about 0.35.

issues.problem: Travel after release is unbounded compared with the plate. MAX_SPEED is 14 × 1.25 = 17.5 px per frame and the decay is a pure exponential with τ 1.4s, so a fast swipe keeps carrying content about v·τ·60 ≈ 1,470 buffer px, more than twice the plate width. Even the intro swipe, peaking near 9.6 px per frame, carries the band centre about 800px. Within 1 to 2 seconds the band is flushed into long streaks of edge pixels, so the plate shows a streak wash instead of A's shapes in stair-stepped slabs taking on B's colours.
issues.fix: Use a 'tear then melt' damping in stepField: `const damp = Math.exp(-dt / params.persistence) / (1 + 0.35 * Math.hypot(vx, vy) * dt * 60 / maxSpeed);` applied per cell. Cap MAX_SPEED at about 9. High speeds then shed fast, a big initial tear, and the low-speed tail lingers for seconds, a slow melt. Total travel lands around 200 to 300 buffer px.

issues.problem: The vector ticks, the skeptic's main upgrade, only show while pressed && engaged. On release they fade within about 250ms while the slabs keep sliding for seconds, so the visitor loses sight of the vectors that are causing the melt.
issues.fix: Let the field target stay at 1 while energy > 0.6 after a drag: `const fieldTarget = params.vectors || (pressed && engaged) || (afterDrag && energy > 0.6) ? 1 : 0;`. Set afterDrag in drag() and clear it in completeKey/settle, so the ticks visibly shrink as the motion decays.

issues.problem: Pressing gives no feedback. The surface sets data-pressed but no CSS reads it, and the lens only grows once a drag has engaged. A press that hasn't moved yet shows nothing for 260ms until the freeze ring appears.
issues.fix: In easeOverlays, grow the lens on press: radiusTarget = pressed ? LENS_PRESS_BLOCKS : LENS_HOVER_BLOCKS, with lensTarget = 1 on press. Alternatively add `.mosh-surface[data-pressed="true"] { cursor: grabbing; }` and a 150ms press scale on the ring.

issues.problem: The 40-frame presim runs synchronously inside one IntersectionObserver or rAF task: 40 full advect passes plus 40 generateMipmap calls on RGBA16F at 640² (512² on phones). That is a single long GPU stall just as the CSS blur entrances run, so on phones the side-panel rise stutters.
issues.fix: Spread the presim over the first few rAFs, for example 10 frames per tick for 4 ticks, before calling onReady. Or run the presim with mip generation only on the last frame, since the residual gate reads mips: give simulate a mips flag and generate only when the residual or ringing is non-zero for that frame.

issues.problem: Each pointermove calls getBoundingClientRect right after the previous move wrote --ring-x/--ring-y, which forces a style recalc on every event. toBuffer and normalise also allocate arrays on every event.
issues.fix: Cache the rect at pointerdown and in the ResizeObserver callback (store it in a ref), then compute normalised coordinates from the cached rect. Write the ring position with a single transform string.

issues.problem: Only 3 covers load eagerly. After the second keyframe the next target hasn't been fetched, so for the first 100 to 300ms of the following drag hasTarget is false and moving blocks take on no colour. That is the one moment the visitor tests the mechanic again.
issues.fix: After seed(), call requestCover for every index (only decode; uploads stay gated by `wanted`), so all six images are decoded before the visitor reaches them.

issues.problem: Changing the block size plays playSwipe(value) with 8, 16 or 32, and all of those are 0 mod 4, so it is always the same swipe. allocateField also zeroes the live field at once, so a mosh in progress stops dead (an instant state swap).
issues.fix: Pass BLOCK_SIZES.indexOf(value) + 1 to playSwipe. In allocateField, resample the old velocity field into the new grid (nearest-cell copy) instead of zeroing it.

issues.problem: The fallback captions read 'Card 01 — Local scans', which looks like placeholder slop whenever Spotify is unavailable, for example in dev without a token.
issues.fix: Use the real names from public/flyout/CREDITS.md, for example { title: 'Honus Wagner', artist: 'T206, 1909' }, { title: 'Ty Cobb', artist: 'T206, 1909' }, and so on.

issues.problem: The kbd chip uses text-ui-xs (14px leading) with 4px padding, so it is 22px tall and the Keyframe button 30px, which is off the 4px grid. The button also shows 'Space' on touch devices, which have no keyboard. The ring box-shadow hard-codes rgb(255 255 255 / 0.9), and several radii use 999px instead of --radius-full.
issues.fix: Give .mosh-key__kbd `line-height: 1; height: 20px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center;`, which makes the button 28px. Add `@media (pointer: coarse) { .mosh-key__kbd { display: none; } }`. Use var(--color-surface-raised) for the ring halo and var(--radius-full) for the pills.

issues.problem: padding-top: 4px only applies when the drawer is open, so it snaps in while the grid-rows transition runs and the first row jumps by 4px.
issues.fix: Keep padding-top: 4px on .mosh-codec__inner all the time. The 0fr row hides it while closed anyway.

critique.wowGap: Make the motion 'tear, then melt', in two parts. First, in stepField replace the pure exponential decay with speed-dependent damping, v *= exp(-dt/τ) / (1 + 0.35·|v|·dt·60/maxSpeed), and cap MAX_SPEED at about 9. A fast swipe then rips the cover into hard stair-stepped slabs over its first 150ms, and the field keeps a long 0.5 to 1 px-per-frame tail that drifts for seconds. A's shapes stay legible while the gated DC residual pours B's colours into each 16px square. Second, keep the round-capped vector ticks visible while that tail decays. Today the band flushes into edge streaks within a second and the colour transfer reads as a pixelated crossfade, which is the generic-glitch failure the brief warned about. (Fix the StrictMode canvas blocker first, or Herb never sees any of it.)

changes: MoshStage.jsx (blocker): removed the JSX <canvas>. Each effect run now creates its own canvas (class mosh-canvas, aria-hidden), prepends it to the surface, and removes it after engine.dispose() and on a construction error. StrictMode and reduced-motion re-runs now get a fresh WebGL2 context instead of a lost one.

moshEngine.js resize(): repaints right after applyResolution when active, seeded, past the presim and the context is not lost, so resizing no longer flashes a black frame. render() already skips the reveal bookkeeping once reveal is 1.

moshEngine.js stepField (wowGap, tear then melt): MAX_SPEED drops from 14 to 9. Per-cell damping is now exp(-dt/τ) / (1 + 0.35·max(0,|v| − 0.75·scale)·frames/maxSpeed): fast blocks shed speed hyperbolically (the tear), and below about 0.75 px/frame only the persistence τ acts, so a slow melt lasts about 2s. Energy now goes to 0 when the field snaps to rest.

moshShader.js ADVECT: codec ringing is now a per-macroblock event rather than a blend. A uint hash of (block, uFrameCount) is compared with ringGate, and on a hit the block takes a full step quantised to 20/255 (half of the AC difference to the target, ×(1, 0.5, 0.5)). The engine passes a new uFrameCount int that increases every frame.
moshParams.js: default ringing goes from 0.6 to 0.35, MPEG-2 from 1 to 0.8 and Bloom from 0.4 to 0.2. The engine's built-in defaults match.

moshEngine.js vector ticks (wowGap): a new afterDrag flag is set in drag() and cleared in beginKey, completeKey and settle, and also once motion comes to rest. The field stays visible through the whole melt tail and fades only when motion stops.
moshShader.js DISPLAY: tick length is now sqrt(speed / uTickFull) × 0.44 block (uTickFull replaces uTickGain), so ticks shrink visibly with the slow tail instead of collapsing straight to dots.
Press feedback: setPressed(true) shows the lens and grows it to the press radius right away, before any drag. CSS adds cursor: grabbing on .mosh-surface[data-pressed=true].

Presim: the 40 intro frames now run 10 per animation frame over 4 frames (runPresim). Nothing is drawn until they finish, onReady fires after the last batch, and drag, pan, swipe and keyframe are ignored until then (playable()).

Pointer path: the surface rect is cached at pointerdown, cleared by the ResizeObserver and by a passive capture scroll listener, and read lazily. unitX/unitY and the inline buffer maths replace the allocating normalise and toBuffer. The ring moves with a single style.translate write, positioned by CSS left/top at −2 blocks, which also fixes scale skewing its position.
Cover loading: after seed() every cover is requested for decode, while uploads stay gated by `wanted`. Only the current and target covers load eagerly before that.

Block size: changing it plays playSwipe(BLOCK_SIZES.indexOf(value) + 1), so each size gets a different swipe. allocateField resamples the old velocity field into the new grid by nearest cell and keeps energy, so a mosh in progress carries on.
page.js: the fallback covers carry real card names and sets from CREDITS.md (Honus Wagner, T206, 1909; Ty Cobb; … King Kelly, Old Judge, 1889).

mosh.css: the kbd chip is a 20px inline-flex with line-height 1 and the Keyframe button a fixed 28px, both on the 4px grid. The kbd is hidden on pointer: coarse. The ring halo uses var(--color-surface-raised), every 999px radius is now var(--radius-full), and .mosh-codec__inner keeps padding-top: 4px whether open or closed.
experiment.json: shorter two-sentence description in the voice of list.js, updated intent, tags kept, building false, status candidate.
polish.remaining: The three checks were run and all print PASS: lab-gate, compile-check (7 modules) and glsl-check (4 shaders). Nothing ran in a browser, as the task required, so the behaviour is traced by hand, not seen on screen. The constants for tear then melt (TEAR_DRAG 0.35, MELT_SPEED 0.75, ringing 0.35 with a half step per event) are tuned on paper and may need a look at localhost /taste. Stored params in localStorage from the earlier build, such as ringing 0.6, will no longer match the H.264 preset until Reset is pressed.

recheck.firstFrame: The server render shows the Swiss side panel rising in with a blur stagger, next to an empty plate: a pulsing dot grid on surface-sunken, with no cover art yet. After hydration the stage loads, two 640px covers decode, and 40 frames are pre-simulated in four rAF batches. The canvas then fades in on paper (#e9edf3, which matches surface-sunken) and depixelates from the top-left in a diagonal mip ladder over 900ms. That reveals cover A with a top-left to bottom-right band: 16px blocks dragged about 150 buffer px along the swipe in stair-stepped whole-pixel seams. The band carries a flat per-block DC shift toward B's colours (about 60%) plus scattered hard 20/255 4px ringing blocks, and B's real pixels pull in at the edges. The band keeps melting at about 1px per frame for roughly 2s, then holds. This is close to the brief and reads as a codec, not a blur. Two things weaken it: the plate sits empty or as paper for the whole decode wait, and the motion-vector ticks, the codec signature, are absent from the first frame.
recheck.checks: All three pass. lab-gate mosh: PASS. lab-compile-check mosh: PASS (7 modules). lab-glsl-check src/app/lab/mosh: ok for moshShader.js:10 (ENCODE), :29 (ADVECT) and :119 (DISPLAY). Previous round: all four findings are verified fixed. (1) StrictMode blocker: the canvas is now created inside the effect, prepended to the surface, and removed after dispose(), so each run gets a fresh context. (2) Resize flash: resize() now renders straight away when seeded, active and presim is done. (3) Ringing: it is now a per-block event via a uint hash of block and uFrameCount, gated by smoothstep(3,6,speed)*rate, with the full quantised step. Default ringing is 0.35. (4) Tear then melt: damp = exp(-dt/tau)/(1+0.35*frames*max(0,|v|-melt)/maxSpeed), and MAX_SPEED is 9 (11.25 at the 640 buffer). Simulated: an 11.25 px/frame release travels about 158px over 2.6s, with only about 15 frames above the residual gate of 2px/frame.

issues.problem: With fieldShow at 1 (every drag, the 2.6s melt tail after a drag, or the Show vectors toggle), every macroblock draws a tick, including still ones, where tip equals centre so the tick is a 1.7px dot. The whole plate gets a 40x40 dot lattice at about 19 css px spacing over the art. ffmpeg vis_mv draws nothing for zero vectors. The lattice reads as a debug grid laid on the cover, not as vectors pushing slabs.
issues.fix: Weight the field ink by speed and keep the always-on dots only inside the hover lens: `float moving = smoothstep(0.15, 0.5, speed); float show = max(uFieldShow * moving, lens) * step(0.999, revealLocal);`. Only moving blocks then grow round-capped ticks.

issues.problem: The intro swipe and its melt never show the vector field, because tailShowing requires afterDrag and the script never sets it. The first frame, the vote, has none of the codec debug ticks that Herb's skeptic named as the thing that separates this from a glitch filter.
issues.fix: Set `afterDrag = true` where seed() starts the intro script (line 485), and in playSwipe too. Combined with speed-gated ticks, the band in the first frame carries ink arrows that shrink and fade as the slabs settle.

issues.problem: Until the covers decode, the plate is a pulsing dot-grid placeholder, then it reveals from flat paper. On a cold Spotify CDN fetch that is a visibly empty plate on the first frame. The brief asked for the first cover's average colour.
issues.fix: Server-render cover A as the placeholder. Always set `--mosh-fallback` to stream[0].image, give .mosh-placeholder `background: var(--mosh-fallback) center / cover` with no pulse, and let the canvas's depixelating reveal land on top of it. The plate is then never empty.

issues.problem: When the stage effect re-runs, for example when the OS reduced-motion setting is toggled, a fresh engine starts at current 0 and target 1 but never emits onCovers. React's state can still point at another cover, so the caption, chips and underline disagree with the plate. `ready` also stays true, so the new canvas is shown at opacity 1 before it is seeded, a blank flash, and the counter keeps its old value.
issues.fix: Call `callbacks.onCovers?.({ current, target })` and `callbacks.onFrames?.(0, true)` once at the end of createMoshEngine. In MoshExperience, setReady(false) in handleApi when api is null, so data-ready drops on teardown and the canvas only fades in after the new presim.

issues.problem: On the standalone page, arrow keys pressed with focus on body are preventDefault-ed into pans. Below 900px the page is taller than the viewport (controls under the plate), so keyboard users cannot arrow-scroll the page.
issues.fix: Handle arrows only when origin === surface, and keep Space on body as the page-level shortcut. Alternatively, only accept body-level arrows when the plate is fully in view.

issues.problem: Covers carry only imageLarge (640px). The 40px chips paint it as a CSS background, a no-cors request, while the engine fetches the same URL with crossOrigin anonymous. Chrome keys those requests separately, so each of the six large images can download twice, and the chips decode 640px images for 40px tiles.
issues.fix: Keep both URLs on each cover, `{ image: track.imageLarge ?? track.image, thumb: track.image }`. Use `thumb` for `--chip-image` in MoshExperience.jsx:444.

issues.problem: In the 296px desktop side column, the preset row is 1fr next to the Tune button. That leaves each of the 4 segments about 44px of content width after its 4px padding. 'MPEG-2' at 13px (text-ui) measures about 46 to 48px and is white-space nowrap, so it likely spills past its pill into 'Bloom'.
issues.fix: Put the Tune toggle on its own row below the presets (grid-template-columns: 1fr), or widen --mosh-side to 312px, or set the option padding to 4px 0.

issues.problem: The freeze ring pops in on --ease-overshoot (cubic-bezier 0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), so it bounces. Taste rule: nothing bounces unless the mechanic is a bounce, and pinning blocks is not one.
issues.fix: Use `scale 240ms var(--ease-entrance)` for the on state.

issues.problem: The failure copy 'This plate needs WebGL2, so here is the cover as it was played.' is awkward. With the flyout fallback it also shows baseball cards under a 'Now playing' label.
issues.fix: Use 'Mosh needs WebGL2. Showing the cover untouched.' For the fallback set, label the section 'Now showing' when covers come from FALLBACK_COVERS: pass a `source` prop from page.js.

recheck.wowGap: Make the first frame show the codec, not just its result. Gate the tick ink by block speed (`show = max(uFieldShow * smoothstep(0.15, 0.5, speed), lens)`) so only moving blocks draw round-capped ink arrows and still blocks draw nothing. Then set afterDrag = true when the intro script and the embedded or preset swipes start. On load, the diagonal reveal resolves into cover A with a band of ink motion vectors visibly shoving 16px slabs down-right in B's colours. The arrows shrink to dots and fade as the melt tail dies over about 2s. That lands the ffmpeg vis_mv signature in the vote frame, and today it only appears after the visitor has already dragged.

changes: moshShader.js: tick ink is gated by block speed (show = max(uFieldShow * smoothstep(0.15, 0.5, speed), lens)), so still blocks draw nothing and the 40x40 dot lattice is gone; ticks now fade in with the last reveal rung instead of popping on a step

moshShader.js: ticks are now round-capped ink arrows, a thin shaft with a round bulb at the tip that grows with reach; length follows pow(speed/full, 0.4) and TICK_FULL_SPEED drops 5 to 4, so slow melt vectors still read as arrows before they shrink to dots and fade

moshEngine.js: afterDrag = true when seed() starts the intro script and in playSwipe, so the intro band and the embedded and preset swipes carry the vis_mv vector field in the first frame and through the melt tail

moshEngine.js + moshShader.js: unrevealed reveal cells now show cover A's own texture (held until the reveal ends, then evicted) instead of flat paper, so the canvas fades in identical to the placeholder and the diagonal mip ladder decodes the cover into the moshed band; PAPER/uPaper/setVec3 removed
moshEngine.js: createMoshEngine emits onCovers({current, target}) and onFrames(0, true) on creation, so a re-run stage resyncs caption, chips, underline and counter
MoshExperience.jsx: handleApi(null) sets ready false, so on stage teardown data-ready drops and the new canvas only fades in after its presim (no blank flash)

MoshExperience.jsx + mosh.css: the placeholder is a server-rendered of the current cover (crossOrigin anonymous, fetchPriority high, so the engine's CORS fetch reuses it), blurring and scaling in; the pulsing dot grid and the --mosh-fallback var are gone, and the plate is never empty, including in the WebGL2 failure state
MoshStage.jsx: arrow-key pans only fire when the plate has focus; Space on body stays the page-level keyframe shortcut, so arrows scroll the page again
page.js: covers carry image (imageLarge) and thumb (300px); MoshExperience chips paint thumb, which ends the duplicate 640px downloads and decodes
page.js + MoshExperience.jsx: source prop ('recent' or 'fallback'); the flyout fallback labels the section 'Now showing'
MoshExperience.jsx: failure copy is now 'Mosh needs WebGL2. Showing the cover untouched.'
mosh.css: the Tune toggle sits on its own row under the full-width presets (about 72px per segment), so 'MPEG-2' no longer spills into the next pill
mosh.css: the freeze ring on-state uses scale 240ms var(--ease-entrance) instead of overshoot; the chip pop drops its 1.02 overshoot keyframe
polish2.remaining: Not checked in a browser, per the rules. These were traced by hand: tick legibility at the vote frame (the melt is around 0.4 to 0.9 px/frame when the reveal finishes, so arrows are short and fading by then), the seam between the CSS object-fit cover and the canvas's centre-crop cover texture, and whether Spotify's CDN serves the server-rendered crossOrigin img from cache for the engine's fetch. experiment.json already had building: false and a complete title, description, tags and intent, so it was left unchanged.

build.summary: Tear-off is a flat paper roll at the left edge of a light table. It feeds out a strip of tickets printed with Herb's real recently played covers, each with a title, artist, No. 014, duration, 'Admit one' and a barcode hashed from the track id. Each ticket is a DOM element whose edge is an SVG paper path with real perforation holes. Physics is a hand-written 2D XPBD rigid-body solver in xpbd.js with 10 substeps, 11 compliant bridge constraints per seam, rigid edge contact so a twist pivots on the far corner, plastic yield, a braked one-way roll that unspools on a slow pull, a soft damped hand for strip grabs and a rigid one for stubs. Bridges break on either elastic (force) or geometric stretch, each with its own seeded strength. Under load the holes stretch into ovals and the bridges thin out. A broken bridge leaves soft ragged nubs, split 30–70% between the two sides, and the path is redrawn in the same frame. Tearing a ticket off rolls a SlotNumber count, plays a paper tick per bridge (WebAudio bandpassed noise) or four quick bursts for a yank, and starts that track's 30s preview through /api/spotify/preview. The ticket's barcode sweeps in the audio purple as the preview plays. Then the roll turns and feeds the next real track out on --ease-entrance.
build.wowMoment: On load the roll spins and feeds the strip out. The end ticket then twists by itself, and its perforation unzips from the top one bridge at a time until two are left, so it sits about 5° skewed with an open wedge. When you twist it the holes stretch into ovals and the bridges thin out before each one parts with its own tick. Yanking it breaks all eleven in one frame. The torn stub skates into a neat pile and starts playing that song's preview.
build.knownIssues:
Not checked in a browser, as instructed. All three checks pass (lab-gate, compile-check, glsl-check reports no shaders), and check-type-system lists nothing for this folder. Behaviour was verified in two ways. Node simulations of xpbd.js, from runs before the last tuning changes: a slow twist tears bridges one by one in seeded order, from the side being pulled; a slow straight pull (200–400 px/s) unspools the roll without tearing; a yank or a pull of about 700 px/s or faster breaks all 11 within one or two frames; a thrown stub stops and sleeps. An end-to-end run of the engine in a hand-made fake DOM covered the intro feed, the intro twist, a twist tear, a yank, a pull to the six-ticket limit, the wind-back spring, Enter/Backspace/ArrowRight, New roll, nine tears in a row with stubs trimmed at 8, idle with no rAF running, no NaN, and destroy leaving the stage empty.

Deviations from the brief: torn edges are an inline SVG path whose d is rewritten, not a CSS mask data-URI (the skeptics flagged hitching). Bridge stiffness, roll brake and hand compliance use my own calibrated values, because the brief's numbers cannot tear. On phones (under 640px) only about 1.5 strip tickets fit, not 3. The intro twist leaves 2 bridges intact at about 5°, not 6° with 2 open. Releasing a strip ticket freezes its pose so a partial tear stays visible. 'Admit one' is hidden on small tickets. The scripted Enter tear steers the stub toward the pile and a neat angle.

Risks: Safari may reject the preview play() started mid-drag; it retries on pointerup, but a slow preview lookup can stay silent. The fallback covers now carry Please Please Me titles, but the /flyout images are not that album's art. Rotated DOM text may soften while moving (will-change is dropped 8 frames after rest so it re-rasterises crisp). Fine-tuning the tear feel (RAIL_BRAKE, RAIL_VISCOUS, bridge limits in xpbd.js) will need a real pointer.

critique.firstFrame: The server render and the first paint show only the h1 "Tear-off", a one-line instruction, "2 torn", the sound toggle and "New roll" on an empty light table. After hydration the outlined roll blurs in over 640ms. The tickets wait in queue.whenReady for the first 9 covers (up to 2.2s). The roll then feeds a strip of 5 tickets (2 on a phone) out at -4° over 900ms, and two stubs with torn edges pop in at the bottom right. About 140ms later the tease twists the end ticket. In my simulation of that exact script, it breaks 9 of the 11 bridges at about 5.4° and stops. At rest at about 2s the composition is strong: a pastel ticket strip with real covers, the end ticket twisted and hanging by its two bottom bridges, and stubs piled at the bottom right. But it takes about 2 seconds to get there, and the demo has already done 80% of the tear the user was supposed to do.
critique.checks: 1. lab-gate tear-off: PASS. 2. compile-check tear-off: PASS (8 modules). 3. glsl-check: no shaders found (a pure DOM/SVG piece, so the check does not apply). I also ran xpbd.js headless in a Node harness (scratchpad/tearsim/sim*.mjs) with the desktop layout (W=320, H=136, 5 tickets). Results: a slow straight pull at 150-600px/s unspools the roll and does not tear. A yank at 1000px/s or more breaks all 11 bridges within 1-2 frames, at both 60 and 120Hz. Dragging a corner down at 30px/s unzips progressively from k0 to k10 over 500ms. If you stop mid-tear, the tear holds at 5 broken with loads stable. The Enter-key scripted tear frees the ticket at about 500ms and the last bridge pops on its own. The tease breaks 9 of 11 bridges.

issues.problem: The intro tease spends the wow moment. With TEASE_TWIST=8° and TEASE_BREAKS=9, the simulation breaks k0 to k8 by 500ms and leaves the end ticket hanging by two bridges. The user's first touch then snaps those last two, so they get 2 ticks and never feel the zip on the ticket they see first. The brief asked for only the last two bridges to be open. Even a 2° twist breaks 5, because the top bridges fail in a burst.
issues.fix: Set TEASE_BREAKS = 2 and TEASE_TWIST = 3 * Math.PI / 180. The script already ends the moment the threshold is reached, so it freezes with exactly k0 and k1 open (the first breaks land together at about 450ms) and the other bridges visibly loaded and pinched.

issues.problem: onPointerDown returns early with `if (script) return;`. A press during the tease, which runs roughly 1.2-2.1s after load, or during an Enter tear is swallowed. The ticket ignores the user's first grab, at exactly the moment they are most likely to reach for it.
issues.fix: Before the early return, interrupt a tease: `if (script && script.kind === 'tease') endScript(false);`. Then fall through to the normal grab, and only block while a 'tear' script is mid-fling. The grab already cancels an intro tween the same way.

issues.problem: The meta row ('No. 014' + duration + 'Admit one', nowrap, gap 12) is about 155px wide at 12px. Between a 640px and 1207px viewport, W shrinks to 220-318px and the text column to 92-146px. 'Admit one' then overflows into the barcode and, at 1024px, past the ticket's perforated edge. This hits iPad and small laptops.
issues.fix: Drop 'Admit one' completely, which also removes the fake-vintage pastiche both skeptics warned about. If it stays, hide it whenever W < 300 by setting stage.dataset.size to 'md' in computeLayout. Either way, add overflow: hidden to .to-ticket__meta.

issues.problem: The first paint is an empty table. Tickets are not created until the first 9 covers decode (up to a 2.2s timeout), then a 120ms delay plus a 900ms feed. The composed frame arrives about 1.5-3s after the page appears, so the first frame, which is the vote, is just text and a roll outline.
issues.fix: Build the roll immediately with FALLBACK_TINT and empty cover wells (the and the tint fill transition already fade in). Await only the first 4 visible covers with a 600ms timeout before starting the feed, and drop the 120ms intro delay.

issues.problem: On a 390px phone W is 226 and restEnd about 339px, so buildRoll makes only 2 strip tickets: one full ticket plus half of one coming out of the roll. It does not read as a roll of tickets, and the brief asks for 3 visible.
issues.fix: For small layouts use W = clamp(width * 0.44, 168, 196) and a steeper axis, about -14°, starting lower: mouthY around height * 0.30 and restEnd measured along the diagonal. That fits about 2.5 tickets. Alternatively, put the roll at the top and feed the strip downward.

issues.problem: In the zip, the first half goes at a speed the user cannot control. At a slow 30px/s corner drag, k0 to k4 break on 5 consecutive frames (66ms), then k5 to k10 spread over 450ms. Bridge strengths vary only ±12-18%, and the ductile yield loads all the top bridges together, so the first half rattles off as one burst rather than hole by hole.
issues.fix: Widen the seeded strength: bridgeLimitG = 2.25 * (0.7 + random() * 0.6). Lower the plastic flow (YIELD_STRETCH around 1.6) so the far bridge fails while its neighbours are still elastic. Optionally add 15% of a broken bridge's load to the next intact neighbour's measured load for a few frames, so each break hands off visibly.

issues.problem: Every intact bridge is stroked by both neighbouring tickets with the 18% ink hairline (the L segments along x=W and x=0). The perforation reads as a cut line between separate cards butted together, not as continuous paper bridges that are about to part.
issues.fix: Use two paths per ticket: the fill as now, and a stroke path with only the top and bottom edges, hole arcs and nubs, where intact bridge segments become M moves instead of L. A bridge then shows no line until it is loaded and pinches.

issues.problem: After you pull to unspool the roll and let go, runFeed sees delta < -0.25W and springs the strip back into the roll. That is a rubber band on a ratcheted paper roll, and it undoes the user's pull.
issues.fix: On release, only feed forward (delta > 2). Leave an over-pulled strip where it is, or snap it to the nearest whole-ticket position on --ease-entrance. Keep the spring wind-back for Backspace only.

issues.problem: Any width change over 1px, including window resizes, phone rotation or a scrollbar appearing, rebuilds the whole scene after 140ms. It throws away the user's pile, restarts numbering at 014 and recreates the two fake stubs, but `count` is left at, say, '7 torn', so the counter no longer matches what is on the table.
issues.fix: Rebuild only when the computed W changes. Otherwise re-run computeLayout and re-anchor the strip's railX/railY to the new mouth while keeping the stubs (clamp them into the new bounds). When a rebuild does happen, reset count to INITIAL_TORN and call onCount.

issues.problem: `playingTicket` keeps the full tick (10 XPBD substeps, render, roll spin) running every frame for the whole 30s preview, only to write the barcode's --to-play progress. The idle sleep is defeated whenever a song plays.
issues.fix: Once the audio's duration is known, set --to-play with a CSS animation (animation-duration = remaining seconds, linear, paused on stop), or drive it from a separate tiny rAF that writes only that property, and drop playingTicket from `busy`.

issues.problem: Pressing a strip ticket gives no feedback until the bridges start to stretch. The 1.02 lift is limited to stubs, so the first press on the end ticket looks dead.
issues.fix: On pointerdown of a strip ticket, put a small preload of about 0.15 on the left seam's bridgeLoad and mark the seam dirty, so the holes ovalise and the bridges pinch slightly, then release it on pointerup. That is tension shown before failure, with no scale.

issues.problem: A stub's aria-label says 'Enter plays a preview', but updateTabStops gives every stub tabIndex -1, so keyboard users cannot reach them. The sound toggle also changes aria-label and sets aria-pressed at the same time, which gives screen readers a double meaning.
issues.fix: Make stubs reachable with a roving tabIndex (arrow keys cycle through the pile), or drop the claim from the label. Keep the toggle's aria-label constant ('Sound') and rely on aria-pressed alone.

issues.problem: The instruction line under the h1 explains a mechanic the tease is already demonstrating. The lab contract asks for a one-line title and nothing else, and Herb dislikes micro-labels that explain what is visible.
issues.fix:
Remove the

, or fold a two-to-four word hint into the h1 line (for example 'Tear-off · twist or yank'), and let the corrected 2-bridge tease teach the gesture.

critique.wowGap: Give the zip back to the user's hand. Set TEASE_BREAKS = 2 and TEASE_TWIST = 3°, and let a grab interrupt the tease. The first ticket Herb touches then unzips its 9 remaining bridges tick by tick under his own twist, holds if he pauses, and the preview starts on the last pop. Right now the intro animation performs that moment for him. Pair it with wider per-bridge strength variance (±30%), so the first half of the tear also goes hole by hole instead of 5 bridges in 66ms.

changes: tearOffEngine.js: the tease now uses TEASE_TWIST 3° and TEASE_BREAKS 2. Once the second bridge opens it calls holdSeam, eases the twist back 40% over 260ms and freezes. In a node sim of xpbd.js, 10 of 10 seeds opened exactly k0 and k1 and left the rest visibly pinched (load about 0.4 to 0.85). In 48 sims where the user grabs again, no bridge broke on its own.

tearOffEngine.js: a press during the tease ends it with endScript(false), clears the seam cooldown and falls through to a normal grab. Only a running 'tear' script still blocks the press. The tease also never starts once the user has interacted.

xpbd.js: the zip now goes one hole at a time. Bridge strength varies ±30% for both the elastic and the gap limits, YIELD_STRETCH is 1.6, and each break hands 0.15 extra load to the next intact bridge on each side, fading over 90ms. After a break the seam waits 55ms before the next one, unless that bridge's own stretch is ≥1.6× its limit (a yank). In the sim a 30px/s corner drag now breaks a bridge every 50 to 67ms in order, instead of 5 bridges in 66ms. A yank of 1500px/s or faster still frees all 11 within 1 to 2 frames. Pausing mid-tear holds after at most one more break.

xpbd.js: added setPreload and holdSeam exports and per-seam cooldown and preload arrays. measureSeam now takes the substep h and marks the seam dirty when a bridge's load changes, not only when its gap changes.

tearOffEngine.js: the roll, stubs and strip are built right after mount. Cover wells start as tint placeholders. Only the stub covers and the last 3 strip covers are awaited, with a 600ms timeout, before the 900ms feed. The 120ms intro delay is gone, and the stubs blur in at 60ms and 150ms instead of 460ms.
tearOffEngine.js and tear-off.css: covers sit inside a tinted well and blur in when they load (opacity, blur and scale on --ease-entrance; no transition under reduced motion).
Removed 'Admit one' from the ticket. .to-ticket__meta now has overflow: hidden, and the duration is hidden on small layouts.

computeLayout on phones: W = clamp(width × 0.44, 168, 196), a -14° axis (layout.angle replaces AXIS_ANGLE everywhere), mouthY = max(176 + H, height × 0.3), a 12px margin, and restEnd measured along the diagonal. At 390px this gives about 2.1 tickets out of the roll, up from 1.5. The face uses 8px padding with an H−16 cover and barcode.

ticketPaper.js: paperPath became paperPaths, which returns a fill path and a separate line path. On an attached seam an unloaded bridge is a move (no line); a loaded one draws only its pinched sides. The fill no longer has a stroke, and the new .to-ticket__line carries the hairline and the focus ring.
runFeed only feeds forward on release, so an over-pulled strip stays where it is. The spring wind-back is kept for Backspace and ArrowLeft.

Resize rebuilds only when W changes, and then resets count to INITIAL_TORN and calls onCount. Otherwise reanchor() shifts the strip (rail anchors, followers and an active script) to the new mouth and restEnd, and clamps the stubs into the new bounds.

Preview progress has its own small rAF that writes only --to-play and pauses when the tab is hidden or offscreen. playingTicket is out of `busy` and render(), so the physics loop can sleep while a song plays.
Pressing a strip ticket preloads its left seam by 0.22, so the holes stretch into ovals and the bridges pinch right away. The preload is removed on pointerup.

a11y: stubs use a roving tabIndex (the newest torn stub, or the pile's last) and arrow keys move through the pile. Stub aria-labels mention this. The sound toggle's aria-label is always 'Sound', with aria-pressed alone carrying the state.

TearOffExperience.jsx: removed the instruction

, so the only title is the h1 'Tear-off'.
experiment.json: new description in two sentences, tags Physics, Music and Audio, updated intent, building false, status still candidate.
polish.remaining: All three checks pass. lab-gate printed PASS, compile-check printed PASS (8 modules), and glsl-check found no shaders. The SSR/first-paint frame still has no tickets: they are DOM built by the engine on mount. They now appear immediately on hydration instead of waiting up to 2.2s for covers. Nothing was viewed in a browser, as the rules required. The physics changes were checked with a node simulation of xpbd.js (in the scratchpad tearsim folder) and the engine logic by reading it through. The 3° tease freezes with only about a 1° visible twist, because the twist is backed off 40% so the user's own touch does not snap more bridges. Raising TEASE_RELAX gives a stronger lean but risks a bridge breaking on the user's first touch (at 0.3, 2 of 36 simulated grabs broke one). On a 390px phone about 2.1 tickets are visible, short of the brief's 3.

recheck.firstFrame: SSR paints a light page holding only 'Tear-off' (title-sm, top-left) and the bottom-left chrome ('2 torn' SlotNumber, sound toggle, 'New roll'). The stage stays empty until hydration. On mount the roll and both torn stubs build immediately with the fallback tint: the roll blurs in over 640ms, the stubs pop in at 60 and 150ms, and the covers blur-fade in as they decode. After at most 600ms (await on 3 strip covers plus the stubs) the strip feeds out over 900ms, so the composed frame lands at about 1.2-1.7s, compared with 1.5-3s last round. On desktop at 1440 that is 4 tickets on the -4 deg diagonal coming out of a hairline roll that bleeds off the left edge, plus 2 ragged stubs bottom-right. 140ms later the tease runs. I re-simulated the real xpbd.js in node across 5 seeds: it breaks exactly k0 and k1 at about 420-480ms (one seed reaches 3), then relaxes. The end ticket is left only 0.8-1.0 deg off the strip axis, so the top of the seam opens about 2px, and the remaining bridges are drawn pinched with slightly ovaled holes. That is honest, but at arm's length it reads as a straight, intact strip, not the brief's half-done 6 deg tear. Phone (390x844): W=172, H=72, a -14 deg axis, 2 full tickets plus a 16px sliver at the roll mouth, stubs about 720-750px down, and roughly 400px of empty table between them.
recheck.checks: lab-gate: PASS. lab-compile-check: PASS (8 modules). lab-glsl-check: no shaders found (DOM + SVG + plain-JS XPBD). I also ran the real xpbd.js headless in node (W=320 and W=172) to check feel. A 2000 px/s yank breaks all 11 bridges in one frame. Dragging the top-right corner down at 300px/s unzips all 11 over about 180ms, one or two per frame, while the ticket swings to about 9 deg, which is the gesture people will actually use and it works. A straight pull at 600 px/s or slower does not tear: it unspools the rail by 140-400px. The tear threshold is about 800 px/s.

issues.problem: Any straight pull slower than about 800px/s unspools instead of tearing: 140px at 600px/s, 236px at 80px/s for 3s. On release, runFeed computes delta = restEnd - endRight(), which is negative, so nothing happens and the strip stays over-extended. With a 72px right margin at 1440, a moderate pull leaves the end ticket hanging off the right edge of the viewport. A pointer user cannot get it back: the rail ratchets, and wind-back exists only on Backspace and ArrowLeft. The next tear then has to start from a ticket that is half off-screen. The brief's own risk list says the roll tension must not yank the strip off-screen.
issues.fix: In onPointerUp's strip branch, and in runFeed, retract whenever the strip is over-extended: `const over = endRight() - layout.restEnd; if (over > 4) { startTween(world.rail.s - over, 'spring'); return; }`. This reuses the brief's 420/0.18 wind spring, startTween already sets wind:true so maintainRoll despawns roots that go back into the roll, and the roll lines spin backwards. The result is a tape-measure snap-back, which also teaches that a slow pull feeds and a fast pull tears.

issues.problem: Last round's fix landed exactly as specified (TEASE_BREAKS=2, TEASE_TWIST=3 deg, and a grab now interrupts the tease). In practice it now under-delivers. With only k0 and k1 open, the remaining 9 bridges pin the ticket, and after TEASE_RELAX (0.4) it settles 0.8-1.0 deg off axis, a 2px wedge at the top of a 136px seam. Nubs are 2.4px and holes about 2.5px in radius. The vote frame shows an intact-looking strip, and the 'tear already half done' invitation is lost.
issues.fix: Set TEASE_BREAKS = 4 and TEASE_RELAX = 0.15 (line 44). Simulated across seeds, 4 breaks land the ticket at about 2.5-2.8 deg, a 6-7px wedge with four visible ragged nubs, and still leave 7 bridges, a full zip, for the user's hand. TEASE_TWIST needs no change because the script already stops at the break threshold.

issues.problem: buildRoll appends the stubs before the strip, and the strip is built end-first, so DOM order is stub, stub, end ticket, and so on. The two tabbable tickets are stubStop (the last stub) and the end ticket, so the first Tab lands on a torn stub ('Enter plays a preview'), not on the end ticket as the brief specifies. The stage also comes before the h1 in DOM order, so a screen reader announces the tickets before the title.
issues.fix: Build the strip before the stubs in buildRoll, or after building call `stage.insertBefore(strip[strip.length-1].el, stubs[0]?.el ?? null)`. In TearOffExperience, move <header> above the stage div; it is absolutely positioned, so the layout does not change.

issues.problem: newRoll winds the old strip back with a 620ms tween whose done callback is rebuild. If the user grabs a strip ticket during those 620ms, onPointerDown sets tween = null. Enter has the same effect through beginScript. rebuild then never runs: the stubs are already gone and the count reads 0, but the old strip stays half wound with its old numbers.
issues.fix: When cancelling a tween in onPointerDown or beginScript, check for `tween.done === rebuild-like` and run it immediately. Simpler: give the newRoll tween a flag (`tween.locked = true`) and ignore strip presses while it is set: `if (tween?.locked && ticket.kind === 'strip') return;`.

issues.problem: sound.unlock() is called only in pointerdown and keydown. A pointerdown from touch is not an activation-triggering event (per the HTML spec, only a non-mouse pointerup or touchend is), so on iOS and Android the AudioContext can stay suspended for the first gesture, and the paper ticks of the first tear are silent. resumePending() on pointerup retries only the preview <audio>, not the WebAudio context.
issues.fix: Also call sound.unlock() at the top of onPointerUp. It is idempotent and resumes the context inside a valid gesture.

issues.problem: On a 390x844 phone the strip sits at about y 150-260 and the stubs and pile at about 720-790, leaving about 400px of empty table in the middle of the screen. Only 2 full tickets plus a 16px sliver show, against the brief's 3, though this is better than last round.
issues.fix: Put mouthY at about height * 0.40 for small layouts. Place the pile with y = mouthY + H * 2.4 instead of height - H * 1.5, so strip and stubs read as one composition. Steepening NARROW_AXIS to about -18 deg adds about 30px of run, enough to show a third of the next ticket.

issues.problem: Under a pure rotation about the bottom-left corner, the last intact bridge sits on the pivot, so nothing loads it. In simulation, a 15 deg/s twist opens 9-10 bridges in about 400ms and then the ticket hinges on one bridge to 33-40 deg for 2+ seconds on desktop. On a phone it never lets go within 40 deg. A corner drag that includes some translation tears cleanly, so this only shows for careful twisters, who are exactly the people the brief's wow moment is written for.
issues.fix: In measureSeam, when seamIntact[seam] <= 2, add the relative angle to the strain: `strain += Math.abs(world.a[right] - world.a[left]) / 0.14`. The last bridges then pop by about 8 deg of hinge, and the stub skates off on the final tick.

issues.problem: leave() takes a ticket out of `tickets` and schedules el.remove() with later(). destroy() clears every timer and removes only the elements still in `tickets`. A stub that is leaving when the component unmounts (within 280ms of trimStubs or New roll), or when the covers prop changes or under StrictMode remount, stays orphaned in the stage DOM.
issues.fix: Keep a `leavingEls` Set: add in leave(), delete in the later callback, and in destroy() run `leavingEls.forEach((el) => el.remove())`.

issues.problem: The to-pop entrance overshoots to scale(1.02) at 70%. The brief says stubs land with no bounce, and the taste rule is that nothing bounces unless the mechanic is a bounce.
issues.fix: Drop the 70% keyframe and go straight from 0% (scale .84, blur 6px, opacity 0) to 100% (scale 1). --ease-entrance already gives the soft landing.

issues.problem: Between 640px and 1207px of width, and on any phone rotation, every width change gives a new W, so resize() rebuilds the whole roll.
